title: Naḥw-i Mīr
author: al-Sayyid al-Sharīf al-Jurjānī
subject: nahw
summary: Naḥw-i Mīr is the Persian primer of naḥw ascribed to al-Sayyid al-Sharīf al-Jurjānī (d. 816/1413), the first book of syntax in the madrasas of India, read beside the Mīzān al-ṣarf and before al-ʿAwāmil al-miʾa and Hidāyat al-naḥw. It begins with the word and the sentence and their kinds, the signs of noun, verb and particle, the fixed nouns, the kinds of noun, and the iʿrāb of the noun in sixteen ways and of the muḍāriʿ in four; then come the governors in three chapters, particles, verbs and nouns, with the two abstract governors; and a conclusion on the followers, the diptote and the particles that do not govern. Its examples are short sentences with Zayd and ʿAmr, which the student learns to parse. The lessons follow a Lucknow lithograph of 1884 and explain in English each rule that the Persian gives.

lessons.title: The single word and the compound; the sentence
body: After the ḥamdala the author says what the book is for: a short, well-ordered work of naḥw for the beginner who has already learnt words by heart and “mastered what is most needed of conjugation”, that is, the ṣarf primers. It will show him “the way to how Arabic is put together”, and give him the ability to know iʿrāb and bināʾ and to read “with question and answer”: the madrasa's way of parsing aloud, the teacher asking and the student answering.

Every utterance (lafẓ) used by the Arabs is single (mufrad) or compound (murakkab). The single utterance indicates one meaning and is called a word (kalima). The word is a noun, as rajulun, “a man”; a verb, as ḍaraba, “he hit”; or a particle, as hal, “whether?”, “as has become known in the books of conjugation”: the student has met the three already in ṣarf.

The compound is made of two words or more. It is either conveying (mufīd) or not. The mufīd compound is the one after which, when the speaker falls silent, the hearer has learnt a piece of information or a demand; it is called a sentence (jumla), and also speech (kalām). The sentence is of two divisions: declarative (khabariyya) and non-declarative (inshāʾiyya).

Naḥw-i Mīr starts from the sentence and goes down to the word, where the Ājurrūmiyya starts from speech and the Ṣarf books from the verb. The order suits a book whose aim is to let the beginner take a sentence apart.

the compound: two words or more

the sentence, also called speech (kalām)

tasks.answer: Rajulun: single, a word (a noun). Ghulāmu Zaydin: compound, not conveying; the hearer still waits. Ḍaraba Zaydun: compound and conveying, a sentence.

tasks.prompt: What does the book mean by reading “with question and answer”?
tasks.answer: Parsing aloud: the teacher asks of each word what it is, what governs it and what its iʿrāb is, and the student answers. The book aims to make the beginner able to do this.

tasks.answer: It is called a sentence (jumla) and speech (kalām). It is declarative (khabariyya) or non-declarative (inshāʾiyya).

text.original: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ، وَالْعَاقِبَةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ، وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى خَيْرِ خَلْقِهِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَآلِهِ أَجْمَعِينَ.
text.en: Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds; the [good] end is for the godfearing; and blessing and peace be upon the best of His creation, Muḥammad, and upon all his family.

text.original: اما بعد، بدان أَرْشَدَكَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى که این مختصریست مضبوط در علم نحو، که مبتدی را بعد از حفظ مفردات لغت و معرفت اشتقاق و ضبط مهمات تصریف بآسانی بکیفیت ترکیب عربی راه نماید، و بزودی در معرفت اعراب و بنا و سؤال و جواب خواندن توانائی دهد بِتَوْفِيقِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى وَعَوْنِهِ.
text.en: To proceed. Know — may God Most High guide you — that this is a well-ordered short work on the science of naḥw, which, after [the student] has learnt by heart the single words of the language, come to know derivation and mastered what is most needed of conjugation, easily shows the beginner the way to how Arabic is put together, and soon gives him the ability to know iʿrāb and bināʾ and to read with question and answer, by the help of God Most High and His aid.

text.original: بدانکه لفظ که مستعمل است در سخن عرب بر دو قسمت است: مفرد و مرکب. مفرد لفظی باشد تنها که دلالت کند بر یک معنی، و آن را کلمه گویند، و کلمه بر سه قسمت است: اسم، چون رَجُلٌ، و فعل، چون ضَرَبَ، و حرف، چون هَلْ، چنانکه در تصریف معلوم شده است.
text.en: Know that an utterance (lafẓ) that is used in the speech of the Arabs is of two divisions: single (mufrad) and compound (murakkab). The single is an utterance by itself that indicates one meaning, and it is called a word (kalima). The word is of three divisions: the noun (ism), as rajulun “a man”; the verb (fiʿl), as ḍaraba “he hit”; and the particle (ḥarf), as hal “whether?”, as has become known in [the books of] conjugation.

text.original: اما مرکب لفظی باشد که از دو کلمه یا بیشتر حاصل شده باشد، و مرکب بر دو گونه است: مفید و غیر مفید. مفید آنست که چون قائل بران سکوت کند سامع را خبری یا طلبی معلوم شود، و آن را جمله گویند و کلام نیز، و جمله بر دو قسمت است: خبریه و انشائیه.
text.en: The compound is an utterance that has come about from two words or more. The compound is of two kinds: conveying [a complete meaning] (mufīd) and not conveying it. The mufīd is that which, when the speaker falls silent after it, the hearer learns a piece of information or a demand; it is called a sentence (jumla), and also speech (kalām). The sentence is of two divisions: declarative (khabariyya) and non-declarative (inshāʾiyya).

lessons.title: The declarative sentence: nominal and verbal
body: The declarative sentence (khabariyya) is “that whose speaker can be described as truthful or lying”: it reports something, which is so or is not. It is of two sorts, by its first part. If the first part is a noun, it is a nominal sentence (jumla ismiyya): Zaydun ʿālimun, “Zayd is knowing”. Its first part is the one of whom something is said, the musnad ilayhi, called the mubtadaʾ; its second part is what is said of him, the musnad, called the khabar.

If the first part is a verb, it is a verbal sentence (jumla fiʿliyya): ḍaraba Zaydun, “Zayd hit”. Here the order is reversed: the first part, the verb, is the musnad; the second, Zayd, is the musnad ilayhi, called the fāʿil.

“The musnad is a judgement, and the musnad ilayhi is that about which a judgement is made.” Then a rule about the three kinds of word: the noun can be either, musnad or musnad ilayhi (ʿālimun is musnad, Zaydun musnad ilayhi); the verb can be musnad but never musnad ilayhi, since nothing is said of a verb; and the particle is neither.

These two words, musnad and musnad ilayhi, are the key of the whole book. Every sentence has one of each, and the student who can find them has found the frame of the sentence; the rest are words that follow, govern or complete.

terms.en: the nominal sentence: its first part a noun
the verbal sentence: its first part a verb
that of which something is said: mubtadaʾ or fāʿil
what is said of it: khabar or verb

tasks.prompt: Name the musnad and the musnad ilayhi in Zaydun ʿālimun and in ḍaraba Zaydun.
tasks.answer: In Zaydun ʿālimun, Zaydun is the musnad ilayhi (the mubtadaʾ) and ʿālimun the musnad (the khabar). In ḍaraba Zaydun, ḍaraba is the musnad (the verb) and Zaydun the musnad ilayhi (the fāʿil).

tasks.prompt: Why can a verb never be musnad ilayhi?
tasks.answer: A verb is itself a judgement said of something; nothing can be said of a verb as of a person or a thing. So it is only ever musnad.

tasks.prompt: Why is Zaydun ʿālimun called declarative?
tasks.answer: Its speaker can be called truthful or lying: Zayd either is learned or is not.

text.original: بدانکه جمله خبریه آنست که قائلش را بصدق و کذب صفت توان کرد، و آن بر دو نوع است: اول آنکه جزو اولش اسم باشد، و آن را جمله اسمیه گویند، چون زَيْدٌ عَالِمٌ، یعنی زید داناست؛ جزو اولش مسند الیه است و آن را مبتدا گویند، و جزو دوم مسند است و آن را خبر گویند.
text.en: Know that the declarative sentence is that whose speaker can be described as truthful or lying. It is of two sorts. The first is that whose first part is a noun, and it is called the nominal sentence (jumla ismiyya), as Zaydun ʿālimun, that is, “Zayd is knowing”. Its first part is that to which something is attributed (musnad ilayhi), and it is called the mubtadaʾ; its second part is what is attributed (musnad), and it is called the khabar.

text.original: دوم آنکه جزو اولش فعل باشد، و آن را جمله فعلیه گویند، چون ضَرَبَ زَيْدٌ، یعنی بزد زید؛ جزو اولش مسند است و آن را فعل گویند، و جزو دوم مسند الیه است و آن را فاعل گویند.
text.en: The second is that whose first part is a verb, and it is called the verbal sentence (jumla fiʿliyya), as ḍaraba Zaydun, that is, “Zayd hit”. Its first part is the musnad, and it is called the verb; its second part is the musnad ilayhi, and it is called the fāʿil.

text.original: و بدانکه مسند حکم است، و مسند الیه آنچه بر وی حکم کنند. و اسم مسند و مسند الیه تواند بود، و فعل مسند باشد و مسند الیه نتواند بود، و حرف نه مسند باشد و نه مسند الیه.
text.en: Know that the musnad is a judgement, and the musnad ilayhi is that about which a judgement is made. The noun can be musnad and musnad ilayhi; the verb is musnad and cannot be musnad ilayhi; and the particle is neither musnad nor musnad ilayhi.

lessons.title: The non-declarative sentence (inshāʾ)
body: The non-declarative sentence (inshāʾiyya) is “that whose speaker cannot be described as truthful or lying”: it does not report what is, but brings something about, a command, a question, a wish. Iḍrib, “hit!”, is neither true nor false.

The book counts its kinds with an example each: the command (amr), iḍrib; the prohibition (nahy), lā taḍrib, “do not hit!”; the question (istifhām), hal ḍaraba Zaydun, “did Zayd hit?”; the wish (tamannī), layta Zaydan ḥāḍirun, “would that Zayd were present”; the hope (tarajjī), laʿalla ʿAmran ghāʾibun, “perhaps ʿAmr is absent”.

Then contracts (ʿuqūd), biʿtu wa-shtaraytu, “I have sold and I have bought”, which look like reports but in fact make the sale; calling (nidāʾ), yā Allāhu, “O God”; the offer (ʿarḍ), alā tanzilu bi-nā fa-tuṣība khayran, “will you not stay with us and come by some good?”; the oath (qasam), wa-Allāhi la-aḍribanna Zaydan, “by God, I will surely hit Zayd”; and wonder (taʿajjub), mā aḥsanahu wa-aḥsin bihi, “how fine he is!”.

The contracts are the instructive case. Biʿtu, “I sold”, has the form of a past verb, a report; but said at the sale it is the sale itself, and nobody asks whether it is true. The kind of a sentence is decided by what it does, not by its form.

tasks.prompt: Why is biʿtu, “I sold”, counted as inshāʾ, though it has the form of a past verb?

tasks.prompt: Is Zaydun ʿālimun inshāʾ? Why not?
tasks.answer: No: it reports something that may be true or false. It is a declarative sentence.

text.original: بدانکه جمله انشائیه آنست که قائلش را بصدق و کذب صفت نتوان کرد، و آن بر چند قسم است: امر، چون اِضْرِبْ، و نهی، چون لَا تَضْرِبْ، و استفهام، چون هَلْ ضَرَبَ زَيْدٌ، و تمنی، چون لَيْتَ زَيْدًا حَاضِرٌ، و ترجی، چون لَعَلَّ عَمْرًا غَائِبٌ،
text.en: Know that the inshāʾiyya sentence is that whose speaker cannot be described as truthful or lying. It is of several divisions: the command (amr), as iḍrib “hit!”; the prohibition (nahy), as lā taḍrib “do not hit!”; the question (istifhām), as hal ḍaraba Zaydun “did Zayd hit?”; the wish (tamannī), as layta Zaydan ḥāḍirun “would that Zayd were present”; the hope (tarajjī), as laʿalla ʿAmran ghāʾibun “perhaps ʿAmr is absent”;

text.original: و عقود، چون بِعْتُ وَاشْتَرَيْتُ، و ندا، چون يَا اللَّهُ، و عرض، چون أَلَا تَنْزِلُ بِنَا فَتُصِيبَ خَيْرًا، و قسم، چون وَاللَّهِ لَأَضْرِبَنَّ زَيْدًا، و تعجب، چون مَا أَحْسَنَهُ وَأَحْسِنْ بِهِ.
text.en: contracts (ʿuqūd), as biʿtu wa-ishtaraytu “I have sold and I have bought”; calling (nidāʾ), as yā Allāhu “O God”; the offer (ʿarḍ), as alā tanzilu bi-nā fa-tuṣība khayran “will you not stay with us, and come by some good?”; the oath (qasam), as wa-Allāhi la-aḍribanna Zaydan “by God, I will surely hit Zayd”; and wonder (taʿajjub), as mā aḥsanahu wa-aḥsin bi-hi “how fine he is!”.

lessons.title: The compounds that do not convey: iḍāfa, the number, the name
body: The compound that does not convey leaves the hearer with no information or demand when the speaker stops. It is of three kinds. The first is the iḍāfa compound (murakkab iḍāfī): ghulāmu Zaydin, “Zayd's servant”. The first part is the muḍāf, the second the muḍāf ilayhi, “and the muḍāf ilayhi is always majrūr”.

The second is the compound of bināʾ (murakkab bināʾī): two nouns made one, the second containing the sense of a particle: aḥada ʿashara, “eleven”, to tisʿata ʿashara, “nineteen”, originally aḥadun wa-ʿasharun, “one and ten”; the wāw was dropped and the two became one. Both parts are fixed on the fatḥa, “except ithnā ʿashara, ‘twelve’, whose first part is muʿrab”: ithnā in rafʿ, ithnay in naṣb and jarr.

The third is the compound that keeps the noun from tanwīn (murakkab manʿ-i ṣarf): two nouns made one without the sense of a particle, as Baʿlabakku, Baalbek, and Ḥaḍramawtu. Its first part is fixed on the fatḥa, “in the school of most scholars”, and the second is muʿrab, as a diptote.

“The compound that does not convey is always a part of a sentence”: ghulāmu Zaydin qāʾimun, “Zayd's servant is standing”; ʿindī aḥada ʿashara dirhaman, “I have eleven dirhams”; jāʾa Baʿlabakku, “Baalbek came”. Treat it in the sentence as one word: the whole iḍāfa is the mubtadaʾ, the whole number governs the tamyīz.

tasks.prompt: Which kind of compound is each: ghulāmu Zaydin; tisʿata ʿashara; Ḥaḍramawtu?
tasks.answer: Ghulāmu Zaydin: iḍāfa. Tisʿata ʿashara: of bināʾ (it contains “and”). Ḥaḍramawtu: the compound that keeps from tanwīn (no sense of a particle).

tasks.prompt: Why is ithnā ʿashara an exception?
tasks.answer: In the other compound numbers both parts are fixed on the fatḥa. In ithnā ʿashara the first part is inflected like the dual: ithnā in rafʿ, ithnay in naṣb and jarr.

tasks.prompt: In ghulāmu Zaydin qāʾimun, what is the mubtadaʾ?
tasks.answer: The whole iḍāfa compound ghulāmu Zaydin; within it ghulāmu is in rafʿ as mubtadaʾ and Zaydin in jarr as muḍāf ilayhi. Qāʾimun is the khabar.

text.original: بدانکه مرکب غیر مفید آنست که چون قائل بران سکوت کند سامع را خبری یا طلبی حاصل نشود، و آن بر سه قسم است: اول مرکب اضافی، چون غُلَامُ زَيْدٍ، جزو اول را مضاف گویند و جزو دوم را مضاف الیه، و مضاف الیه همیشه مجرور باشد.
text.en: Know that the compound that does not convey [a complete meaning] is that which, when the speaker falls silent after it, gives the hearer no information or demand. It is of three divisions. First, the iḍāfa compound (murakkab iḍāfī), as ghulāmu Zaydin “Zayd's servant”: the first part is called the muḍāf and the second part the muḍāf ilayhi, and the muḍāf ilayhi is always majrūr.

text.original: دوم مرکب بنائی، و آن آنست که دو اسم را یکی کرده باشند و اسم دوم متضمن حرفی باشد، چون أَحَدَ عَشَرَ تا تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ، که در اصل أَحَدٌ وَعَشَرٌ و تِسْعَةٌ وَعَشَرٌ بوده است، واو را حذف کرده هر دو اسم را یکی کردند، و هر دو جزو مبنی باشد بر فتح، الا اِثْنَا عَشَرَ که جزو اول معرب است.
text.en: Second, the compound of bināʾ (murakkab bināʾī), which is that in which two nouns have been made one and the second noun contains [the meaning of] a particle, as aḥada ʿashara “eleven” up to tisʿata ʿashara “nineteen”, which in origin were aḥadun wa-ʿasharun and tisʿatun wa-ʿasharun: the wāw was dropped and the two nouns were made one. Both parts are mabnī on the fatḥa, except ithnā ʿashara “twelve”, whose first part is muʿrab.

text.original: سوم مرکب منع صرف، و آن آنست که دو اسم را یکی کرده باشند و اسم دوم متضمن حرفی نباشد، چون بَعْلَبَكُّ و حَضْرَمَوْتُ، که جزو اول مبنی باشد بر فتح بر مذهب اکثر علما، و جزو دوم معرب. بدانکه مرکب غیر مفید همیشه جزو جمله باشد، چون غُلَامُ زَيْدٍ قَائِمٌ، وَعِنْدِي أَحَدَ عَشَرَ دِرْهَمًا، وَجَاءَ بَعْلَبَكُّ.
text.en: Third, the compound that keeps [the noun] from tanwīn (murakkab manʿ-i ṣarf), which is that in which two nouns have been made one and the second noun does not contain a particle, as Baʿlabakku Baalbek and Ḥaḍramawtu Ḥaḍramawt: the first part is mabnī on the fatḥa, in the school of most scholars, and the second part is muʿrab. Know that the compound that does not convey [a complete meaning] is always a part of a sentence, as ghulāmu Zaydin qāʾimun “Zayd's servant is standing”, wa-ʿindī aḥada ʿashara dirhaman “and I have eleven dirhams” and wa-jāʾa Baʿlabakku “and Baalbek came”.

lessons.title: The least sentence, and how to take a sentence apart
body: “No sentence is less than two words”, either in wording, ḍaraba Zaydun, Zaydun qāʾimun, or by implication: iḍrib, “hit!”, is one written word, but anta, “you”, is hidden in it, so it is two. There is no upper limit: a sentence may grow without end.

Then the book gives the method of the whole naḥw, in one sentence: when the words of a sentence are many, tell the noun, the verb and the particle apart; see whether each is muʿrab or mabnī; whether it is governor (ʿāmil) or governed (maʿmūl); and see how the words are related to one another, “so that the musnad and the musnad ilayhi appear and the meaning of the sentence is known for certain”.

This is the order in which a student parses aloud. First the kind of each word; then whether its end can change; then what governs what; last, the frame of musnad and musnad ilayhi, which gives the meaning. The rest of the book supplies what each step needs: the signs of the kinds, the fixed and inflected words, the governors.

text.original: بدانکه هیچ جمله کمتر از دو کلمه نباشد، لَفْظًا چون ضَرَبَ زَيْدٌ وَزَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ، یا تَقْدِيرًا چون اِضْرِبْ که أَنْتَ در وی پوشیده است، و ازین بیشتر باشد و بیشتر را حدی نیست.
text.en: Know that no sentence is less than two words, in wording, as ḍaraba Zaydun “Zayd hit” and Zaydun qāʾimun “Zayd is standing”, or by implication, as iḍrib “hit!”, in which anta “you” is hidden. It may be more than this, and the more has no limit.

text.original: بدانکه چون کلمات جمله بسیار باشد اسم و فعل و حرف را با یکدیگر تمییز باید کردن، و نظر نمودن که معرب است یا مبنی، و عامل است یا معمول، و باید دانستن که تعلق کلمات با یکدیگر چگونه است تا مسند و مسند الیه پیدا گردد و معنی جمله بتحقیق معلوم شود.
text.en: Know that when the words of a sentence are many, one must tell the noun, the verb and the particle apart from one another, and look whether [each] is muʿrab or mabnī, and governor (ʿāmil) or governed (maʿmūl); and one must know how the words are related to one another, so that the musnad and the musnad ilayhi appear and the meaning of the sentence is known for certain.

parts.title: The signs of the word; inflected and fixed

lessons.title: The signs of the noun, the verb and the particle
body: The noun has many signs, and the book gives eleven: al- or a particle of jarr at its beginning, al-ḥamdu, bi-Zaydin; tanwīn at its end, Zaydun; being musnad ilayhi, Zaydun qāʾimun; being muḍāf, ghulāmu Zaydin; the diminutive, Qurayshun; the relative adjective in -iyy, baghdādiyyun; the dual, rajulāni; the plural, rijālun; being described, jāʾa rajulun ʿālimun; and the vowelled tāʾ at its end, ḍāribatun.

The verb's signs are fewer: qad before it, qad ḍaraba; the sīn, sa-yaḍribu, or sawfa, sawfa yaḍribu, for the future; a particle of jazm, lam yaḍrib; an attached pronoun in rafʿ joined to it, ḍarabtu, or the quiescent tāʾ, ḍarabat; or being a command, iḍrib, or a prohibition, lā taḍrib.

The two tāʾs are a fine pair. The vowelled tāʾ, as in ḍāribatun, is a sign of the noun; the quiescent tāʾ, as in ḍarabat, is a sign of the verb. The same letter, with a vowel or without, tells two kinds of word apart.

“The sign of the particle is that none of the signs of the noun and the verb is in it.” Hal and fī take no al-, no tanwīn, no qad, no lam: they are particles. One sign is enough to decide: a word with tanwīn is a noun, whatever else it is.

text.original: بدانکه علامت اسم آنست که الف و لام یا حرف جر در اولش باشد، چون اَلْحَمْدُ وَبِزَيْدٍ، یا تنوین در آخرش باشد، چون زَيْدٌ، یا مسند الیه باشد، چون زَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ، یا مضاف باشد، چون غُلَامُ زَيْدٍ، یا مصغر باشد، چون قُرَيْشٌ، یا منسوب باشد، چون بَغْدَادِيٌّ، یا مثنی باشد، چون رَجُلَانِ، یا مجموع باشد، چون رِجَالٌ، یا موصوف باشد، چون جَاءَ رَجُلٌ عَالِمٌ، یا تای متحرک بدو پیوندد، چون ضَارِبَةٌ.
text.en: Know that the sign of the noun is that it has the alif and lām or a particle of jarr at its beginning, as al-ḥamdu “the praise” and bi-Zaydin “with Zayd”; or tanwīn at its end, as Zaydun; or that it is musnad ilayhi, as Zaydun qāʾimun “Zayd is standing”; or muḍāf, as ghulāmu Zaydin “Zayd's servant”; or diminutive, as Qurayshun Quraysh; or relative (mansūb), as baghdādiyyun “of Baghdad”; or dual, as rajulāni “two men”; or plural, as rijālun “men”; or described, as jāʾa rajulun ʿālimun “a learned man came”; or that a vowelled tāʾ is joined to it, as ḍāribatun “hitting (f.)”.

text.original: و علامت فعل آنست که قَدْ در اولش باشد، چون قَدْ ضَرَبَ، یا سین باشد، چون سَيَضْرِبُ، یا سوف باشد، چون سَوْفَ يَضْرِبُ، یا حرف جزم بود، چون لَمْ يَضْرِبْ، یا ضمیر مرفوع متصل بدو پیوندد، چون ضَرَبْتُ، یا تای ساکن، چون ضَرَبَتْ، یا امر باشد، چون اِضْرِبْ، یا نهی باشد، چون لَا تَضْرِبْ. و علامت حرف آنست که هیچ علامتی از علامات اسم و فعل در وی نبود.
text.en: The sign of the verb is that it has qad at its beginning, as qad ḍaraba “he has hit”; or the sīn, as sa-yaḍribu “he will hit”; or sawfa, as sawfa yaḍribu “he will hit”; or a particle of jazm, as lam yaḍrib “he did not hit”; or that an attached pronoun in rafʿ is joined to it, as ḍarabtu “I hit”, or the quiescent tāʾ, as ḍarabat “she hit”; or that it is a command, as iḍrib “hit!”, or a prohibition, as lā taḍrib “do not hit!”. The sign of the particle is that none of the signs of the noun and the verb is in it.

lessons.title: Inflected and fixed; the noun that is firmly placed
body: All the words of the Arabs are inflected (muʿrab) or fixed (mabnī). The muʿrab is “that whose end differs with the difference of the governors”: jāʾanī Zaydun, raʾaytu Zaydan, marartu bi-Zaydin. In the terms of the book, Zayd is the muʿrab, the ḍamma, fatḥa and kasra are the iʿrāb, and the dāl is “the place of the iʿrāb”. The mabnī keeps its end whatever governs it: hāʾulāʾi, “these”, is the same in rafʿ, naṣb and jarr.

Then the book counts the muʿrab, which are few, so that everything else is mabnī. All particles are mabnī; of verbs, the past, the active imperative to the one present, and the muḍāriʿ with the nūn of the feminine plural or the nūn of emphasis are mabnī. So only two things are muʿrab: the noun that is “firmly placed” (mutamakkin), when it stands in a construction, and the muḍāriʿ free of those two nūns.

The noun that is not firmly placed (ghayr mutamakkin) is mabnī, because “it resembles what is mabnī in origin”; and what is mabnī in origin is three things: the past verb, the active imperative to the one present, and all the particles. A pronoun such as the tāʾ of ḍarabtu, a single letter, is like a particle in its build, the commentators say, and so it is fixed like one.

Note the condition “when it stands in a construction” (tarkīb). A noun said alone, as in counting, Zaydun, ʿAmrun, has no governor, and so no iʿrāb yet; it becomes muʿrab when it enters a sentence and a governor acts on it.

text.original: بدانکه همه کلمات عرب بر دو قسم است: معرب و مبنی. معرب آنست که آخرش باختلاف عوامل مختلف شود، چون زید در جَاءَنِي زَيْدٌ، وَرَأَيْتُ زَيْدًا، وَمَرَرْتُ بِزَيْدٍ، پس زید معرب است، و ضمه و فتحه و کسره اعراب، و دال محل اعراب. و مبنی آنست که آخرش باختلاف عوامل مختلف نشود، چون هٰؤُلَاءِ که در حالت رفع و نصب و جر یکسان است.
text.en: Know that all the words of the Arabs are of two divisions: muʿrab and mabnī. The muʿrab is that whose end differs with the difference of the governors, as Zayd in jāʾanī Zaydun “Zayd came to me”, wa-raʾaytu Zaydan “and I saw Zayd” and wa-marartu bi-Zaydin “and I passed by Zayd”: so Zayd is muʿrab, the ḍamma, the fatḥa and the kasra are the iʿrāb, and the dāl is the place of the iʿrāb. The mabnī is that whose end does not differ with the difference of the governors, as hāʾulāʾi “these”, which is the same in the state of rafʿ, naṣb and jarr.

text.original: بدانکه جمله حروف مبنی است، و از افعال فعل ماضی و امر حاضر معروف، و فعل مضارع با نونهای جمع مؤنث و با نونهای تأکید نیز مبنی است. بدانکه اسم غیر متمکن مبنی است، و اما اسم متمکن معرب است بشرط آنکه در ترکیب واقع شود، و فعل مضارع معرب است بشرط آنکه از نونهای جمع مؤنث و نون تأکید خالی باشد. پس در کلام عرب معرب بیش ازین دو قسم نیست، باقی همه مبنی است.
text.en: Know that all the particles are mabnī; and of the verbs, the past verb and the active imperative to the one present, and the muḍāriʿ verb with the nūns of the feminine plural and with the nūns of emphasis, are mabnī too. Know that the noun that is not firmly placed (ghayr mutamakkin) is mabnī, and the noun that is firmly placed (mutamakkin) is muʿrab, on condition that it stands in a construction; and the muḍāriʿ verb is muʿrab, on condition that it is free of the nūns of the feminine plural and the nūn of emphasis. So in the speech of the Arabs there are no more muʿrab than these two divisions; all the rest is mabnī.

text.original: و اسم غیر متمکن اسمیست که با مبنی اصل مشابهت دارد، و مبنی اصل سه چیز است: فعل ماضی و امر حاضر معروف و جمیع حروف. و اسم متمکن اسمیست که با مبنی اصل مشابهت نداشته باشد.
text.en: The ghayr mutamakkin noun is a noun that resembles what is mabnī in origin; and what is mabnī in origin is three things: the past verb, the active imperative to the one present, and all the particles. The mutamakkin noun is a noun that does not resemble what is mabnī in origin.

lessons.title: The fixed nouns (1): the seventy pronouns
body: The noun that is not firmly placed is of eight kinds, and the first is the pronouns (muḍmarāt). The book explains them by Persian glosses: anā, “I”, for a man or a woman; the tāʾ of ḍarabtu, “I hit”, which is “for me in particular”; the yāʾ of ḍarabanī, “he hit me”. Then it counts them: seventy, in five lists of fourteen.

In rafʿ, attached: the endings of the past, ḍarabtu, ḍarabnā, ḍarabta … ḍaraba, ḍarabā, ḍarabū, ḍarabat, ḍarabatā, ḍarabna (in ḍaraba and ḍarabat the doer is hidden). In rafʿ, separate: anā, naḥnu, anta, antumā, antum, anti, antumā, antunna, huwa, humā, hum, hiya, humā, hunna. In naṣb, attached: ḍarabanī, ḍarabanā, ḍarabaka … ḍarabahu, ḍarabahā, ḍarabahunna. In naṣb, separate: iyyāya, iyyānā, iyyāka … iyyāhu, iyyāhā, iyyāhunna. In jarr, attached only: lī, lanā, laka … lahu, lahā, lahunna.

Note the order: Naḥw-i Mīr lists the speaker first, then the one addressed, then the absent, the reverse of the Mīzān's tables, which begin with the absent. And there is no separate pronoun in jarr: a pronoun in jarr is always joined to its particle or its muḍāf.

Five lists, each of fourteen: 5 × 14 = 70. The student recites them as he recited the tables of ṣarf, and with them he can name the iʿrāb of any pronoun: the -hu of ḍarabahu is in naṣb, the -hu of lahu in jarr, though they look the same.

text.original: بدانکه اسم غیر متمکن بر هشت قسمت است. اول مضمرات، چون أَنَا: من، مرد و زن، و ضَرَبْتُ: زدم من، و آن تای خاص مرا، و ضَرَبَنِي: بزد مرا، و آن یای مرا. و این هفتاد ضمیر است:
text.en: Know that the ghayr mutamakkin noun is of eight divisions. First, the pronouns (muḍmarāt), as anā: “I”, man or woman; ḍarabtu: “I hit”, and that tāʾ is for me in particular; and ḍarabanī: “he hit me”, and that yāʾ is for me. These are seventy pronouns:

text.original: چهارده مرفوع متصل: ضَرَبْتُ، ضَرَبْنَا، ضَرَبْتَ، ضَرَبْتُمَا، ضَرَبْتُمْ، ضَرَبْتِ، ضَرَبْتُمَا، ضَرَبْتُنَّ، ضَرَبَ، ضَرَبَا، ضَرَبُوا، ضَرَبَتْ، ضَرَبَتَا، ضَرَبْنَ؛ و چهارده مرفوع منفصل: أَنَا، نَحْنُ، أَنْتَ، أَنْتُمَا، أَنْتُمْ، أَنْتِ، أَنْتُمَا، أَنْتُنَّ، هُوَ، هُمَا، هُمْ، هِيَ، هُمَا، هُنَّ؛
text.en: Fourteen marfūʿ and attached: ḍarabtu “I hit”, ḍarabnā “we hit”, ḍarabta “you (m.) hit”, ḍarabtumā “you two (m.) hit”, ḍarabtum “you (m. pl.) hit”, ḍarabti “you (f.) hit”, ḍarabtumā “you two (f.) hit”, ḍarabtunna “you (f. pl.) hit”, ḍaraba “he hit”, ḍarabā “they two (m.) hit”, ḍarabū “they (m.) hit”, ḍarabat “she hit”, ḍarabatā “they two (f.) hit”, ḍarabna “they (f.) hit”; and fourteen marfūʿ and separate: anā “I”, naḥnu “we”, anta “you (m.)”, antumā “you two (m.)”, antum “you (m. pl.)”, anti “you (f.)”, antumā “you two (f.)”, antunna “you (f. pl.)”, huwa “he”, humā “they two (m.)”, hum “they (m.)”, hiya “she”, humā “they two (f.)”, hunna “they (f.)”;

text.original: و چهارده منصوب متصل: ضَرَبَنِي، ضَرَبَنَا، ضَرَبَكَ، ضَرَبَكُمَا، ضَرَبَكُمْ، ضَرَبَكِ، ضَرَبَكُمَا، ضَرَبَكُنَّ، ضَرَبَهُ، ضَرَبَهُمَا، ضَرَبَهُمْ، ضَرَبَهَا، ضَرَبَهُمَا، ضَرَبَهُنَّ؛ و چهارده منصوب منفصل: إِيَّايَ، إِيَّانَا، إِيَّاكَ، إِيَّاكُمَا، إِيَّاكُمْ، إِيَّاكِ، إِيَّاكُمَا، إِيَّاكُنَّ، إِيَّاهُ، إِيَّاهُمَا، إِيَّاهُمْ، إِيَّاهَا، إِيَّاهُمَا، إِيَّاهُنَّ؛
text.en: fourteen manṣūb and attached: ḍarabanī “he hit me”, ḍarabanā “he hit us”, ḍarabaka “he hit you (m.)”, ḍarabakumā “he hit you two (m.)”, ḍarabakum “he hit you (m. pl.)”, ḍarabaki “he hit you (f.)”, ḍarabakumā “he hit you two (f.)”, ḍarabakunna “he hit you (f. pl.)”, ḍarabahu “he hit him”, ḍarabahumā “he hit them two (m.)”, ḍarabahum “he hit them (m.)”, ḍarabahā “he hit her”, ḍarabahumā “he hit them two (f.)”, ḍarabahunna “he hit them (f.)”; and fourteen manṣūb and separate: iyyāya “me”, iyyānā “us”, iyyāka “you (m.)”, iyyākumā “you two (m.)”, iyyākum “you (m. pl.)”, iyyāki “you (f.)”, iyyākumā “you two (f.)”, iyyākunna “you (f. pl.)”, iyyāhu “him”, iyyāhumā “them two (m.)”, iyyāhum “them (m.)”, iyyāhā “her”, iyyāhumā “them two (f.)”, iyyāhunna “them (f.)”;

text.original: و چهارده مجرور متصل: لِي، لَنَا، لَكَ، لَكُمَا، لَكُمْ، لَكِ، لَكُمَا، لَكُنَّ، لَهُ، لَهُمَا، لَهُمْ، لَهَا، لَهُمَا، لَهُنَّ.
text.en: and fourteen majrūr and attached: lī “for me”, lanā “for us”, laka “for you (m.)”, lakumā “for you two (m.)”, lakum “for you (m. pl.)”, laki “for you (f.)”, lakumā “for you two (f.)”, lakunna “for you (f. pl.)”, lahu “for him”, lahumā “for them two (m.)”, lahum “for them (m.)”, lahā “for her”, lahumā “for them two (f.)”, lahunna “for them (f.)”.

lessons.title: The fixed nouns (2): demonstratives, relatives, nouns of verbs, sounds
lessons.arabic: أَسْمَاءُ الْإِشَارَةِ وَالْمَوْصُولَاتُ وَأَسْمَاءُ الْأَفْعَالِ وَالْأَصْوَاتِ
lessons.transliteration: asmāʾ al-ishāra wa-l-mawṣūlāt wa-asmāʾ al-afʿāl wa-l-aṣwāt
body: The second kind of fixed noun is the demonstratives: dhā for the masculine; dhāni and dhayni for the masculine dual; tā, tī, tihi, dhih, dhihī and tihī for the feminine; tāni and tayni for the feminine dual; and ūlāʾi with madd, or ūlā without, for the plural. The duals change with the state, like duals; the others are fixed.

The third is the relative nouns: alladhī, alladhāni and alladhayni, alladhīna, allatī, allatāni and allatayni, allātī and allawātī; mā, man, ayyun and ayyatun; al- “in the sense of alladhī” in the active and passive participle, al-ḍāribu, al-maḍrūbu; and dhū in the dialect of Ṭayyiʾ, jāʾanī dhū ḍarabaka, “the one who hit you came to me”. The book adds that ayyun and ayyatun are muʿrab: they change, ayyan, ayyin, though they are counted with the fixed.

The fourth is the nouns of verbs (asmāʾ al-afʿāl), in two kinds: in the sense of the imperative to the one present, ruwayda, “gently!”, balha, “leave aside!”, ḥayyahal, “come quickly!”, halumma, “come here!”; and in the sense of the past, hayhāta, “it is far”, shattāna, “how different!”. The fifth is the nouns of sounds (asmāʾ al-aṣwāt): uḥ uḥ, a cough; uf, disgust; bakh bakh, “well done!”; nakh, to make a camel kneel; ghāq, the cry of the crow.

What these kinds share is the reason for their bināʾ: each resembles what is fixed in origin. The demonstrative and the relative need something else to make their meaning clear, a thing pointed at or a ṣila, as a particle needs its noun; the noun of a verb stands in the place of a fixed verb, the imperative or the past.

tasks.prompt: Sort these into demonstratives, relatives and nouns of verbs: tā; allatī; ruwayda; ūlāʾi; man; hayhāta.
tasks.answer: Demonstratives: tā, ūlāʾi. Relatives: allatī, man. Nouns of verbs: ruwayda (as an imperative), hayhāta (as a past).

tasks.prompt: Why is al- in al-ḍāribu counted as a relative noun?
tasks.answer: It means alladhī, “the one who”: al-ḍāribu is “the one who hits”. On a participle, al- is a relative noun, not only the article.

tasks.prompt: Which relative nouns does the book say are muʿrab, and what does that mean?
tasks.answer: Ayyun and ayyatun: their ending changes with the governor (ayyun, ayyan, ayyin), though the other relatives are fixed.

text.original: دوم اسمای اشارات: ذَا، وَذَانِ، وَذَيْنِ، وَتَا، وَتِي، وَتِهِ، وَذِهْ، وَذِهِي، وَتِهِي، وَتَانِ، وَتَيْنِ، وَأُولَاءِ بمد، وَأُولَى بقصر.
text.en: Second, the demonstratives (asmāʾ al-ishārāt): dhā “this (m.)”, dhāni and dhayni “these two (m.)”, tā, tī, tihi, dhih, dhihī and tihī “this (f.)”, tāni and tayni “these two (f.)”, and ūlāʾi, with madd, and ūlā, with qaṣr, “these”.

text.original: سوم اسمای موصوله: اَلَّذِي، وَاللَّذَانِ، وَاللَّذَيْنِ، وَالَّذِينَ، وَالَّتِي، وَاللَّتَانِ، وَاللَّتَيْنِ، وَاللَّاتِي، وَاللَّوَاتِي، وَمَا، وَمَنْ، وَأَيٌّ، وَأَيَّةٌ، و الف و لام بمعنی اَلَّذِي در اسم فاعل و اسم مفعول، چون اَلضَّارِبُ وَالْمَضْرُوبُ، و ذُو بمعنی اَلَّذِي در لغت بنی طی، نحو: جَاءَنِي ذُو ضَرَبَكَ. بدانکه أَيٌّ وَأَيَّةٌ معرب است.
text.en: Third, the relative nouns (asmāʾ mawṣūla): alladhī “who, which (m.)”, alladhāni and alladhayni (m. dual), alladhīna (m. pl.), allatī (f.), allatāni and allatayni (f. dual), allātī and allawātī (f. pl.), mā “what”, man “who”, and ayyun and ayyatun “which”; the alif and lām in the sense of alladhī in the active and the passive participle, as al-ḍāribu “the one who hits” and al-maḍrūbu “the one hit”; and dhū in the sense of alladhī in the dialect of the Banū Ṭayyiʾ, as jāʾanī dhū ḍarabaka “the one who hit you came to me”. Know that ayyun and ayyatun are muʿrab.

text.original: چهارم اسمای افعال، و آن بر دو قسم است: اول بمعنی امر حاضر، چون رُوَيْدَ وَبَلْهَ وَحَيَّهَلْ وَهَلُمَّ، دوم بمعنی فعل ماضی، چون هَيْهَاتَ وَشَتَّانَ. پنجم اسمای اصوات، چون أُحْ أُحْ، وَأُفْ، وَبَخْ بَخْ، وَنَخْ، وَغَاقْ.
text.en: Fourth, the verbal nouns (asmāʾ al-afʿāl), which are of two divisions: first, in the sense of the imperative to the one present, as ruwayda “gently!”, balha “leave aside!”, ḥayyahal “come quickly!” and halumma “come here!”; second, in the sense of the past verb, as hayhāta “it is far” and shattāna “how different!”. Fifth, the nouns of sounds (asmāʾ al-aṣwāt), as uḥ uḥ [a cough], uf [disgust], bakh bakh “well done!”, nakh [to make a camel kneel] and ghāq [the cry of the crow].

lessons.title: The fixed nouns (3): adverbs, allusive nouns, the compound number
body: The sixth kind is some of the adverbs (ẓurūf). Of time: idh, “when” in the past, idhā, “when”, matā, “when?”, kayfa, “how?”, ayyāna, “when?”, amsi, “yesterday”, mudh and mundhu, “since”, qaṭṭu, “ever” in the past, ʿawḍu, “ever” in the future; and qablu and baʿdu, “before” and “after”, when they are muḍāf and the muḍāf ilayhi is dropped and its meaning intended. Of place: ḥaythu, “where”, and quddāmu, taḥtu and fawqu, “in front, below, above”, under the same condition.

That condition matters. Qablu, taḥtu and fawqu are fixed on the ḍamma only when the word they were joined to has dropped but is still meant: min qablu, “before [that]”. When that word is spoken they are inflected: min qabli dhālika. Qaṭṭu goes with the past (mā raʾaytuhu qaṭṭu, “I have never seen him”), ʿawḍu with the future.

The seventh is the allusive nouns (kināyāt), which stand for something not named: kam, “how many”, and kadhā, “so many”, for a number; kayta and dhayta, “such and such”, for talk. The eighth is the compound of bināʾ, aḥada ʿashara, which the book has already explained (lesson 4).

With these eight kinds, pronouns, demonstratives, relatives, nouns of verbs, sounds, adverbs, allusive nouns and compound numbers, the book has listed all the nouns that are fixed. Every other noun is firmly placed and muʿrab.

text.original: ششم اسمای ظروف: ظرف زمان، چون إِذْ وَإِذَا وَمَتَى وَكَيْفَ وَأَيَّانَ وَأَمْسِ وَمُذْ وَمُنْذُ وَقَطُّ وَعَوْضُ وَقَبْلُ وَبَعْدُ، وقتیکه مضاف باشند و مضاف الیه محذوف منوی باشد، و ظرف مکان، چون حَيْثُ وَقُدَّامُ وَتَحْتُ وَفَوْقُ، وقتیکه مضاف باشند و مضاف الیه محذوف منوی باشد.
text.en: Sixth, the adverbs (asmāʾ al-ẓurūf): adverbs of time, as idh “when (past)”, idhā “when”, matā “when?”, kayfa “how?”, ayyāna “when?”, amsi “yesterday”, mudh and mundhu “since”, qaṭṭu “ever (in the past)”, ʿawḍu “ever (in the future)”, and qablu “before” and baʿdu “after” when they are muḍāf and the muḍāf ilayhi is dropped and intended; and adverbs of place, as ḥaythu “where”, quddāmu “in front”, taḥtu “below” and fawqu “above”, when they are muḍāf and the muḍāf ilayhi is dropped and intended.

text.original: هفتم اسمای کنایات، چون كَمْ وَكَذَا کنایت از عدد، و كَيْتَ وَذَيْتَ کنایات از حدیث. هشتم مرکب بنائی، چون أَحَدَ عَشَرَ.
text.en: Seventh, the allusive nouns (asmāʾ al-kināyāt), as kam “how many” and kadhā “so many”, alluding to number, and kayta and dhayta “such and such”, alluding to talk. Eighth, the compound of bināʾ, as aḥada ʿashara “eleven”.

lessons.title: The definite and the indefinite
body: The noun is definite (maʿrifa) or indefinite (nakira). The definite is “laid down for a particular thing”; the indefinite for a thing that is not particular: rajulun, “a man”, farasun, “a horse”.

The definite is of seven sorts: the pronouns; the proper names, Zaydun, ʿAmrun; the demonstratives; the relative nouns, these last two “called the vague nouns (mubhamāt)”; what is made definite by calling, yā rajulu, “O man”; what is made definite by al-, al-rajulu, “the man”; and what is muḍāf to one of these: ghulāmuhu, ghulāmu Zaydin, ghulāmu hādhā, ghulāmu alladhī ʿindī, ghulāmu al-rajuli.

Two of the seven need a word. The demonstratives and relatives are “vague” because by themselves they point to nothing in particular: hādhā is “this” of anything; only the thing pointed at, or the ṣila, makes them clear. And calling makes a noun definite: rajul is indefinite, but yā rajulu said to one man in front of you means that man.

The muḍāf takes the definiteness of what follows it, so the book gives one example for each kind: his servant, Zayd's servant, this one's servant, the servant of the one with me, the man's servant. Joined to an indefinite (ghulāmu rajulin), the noun stays indefinite, only made more particular.

text.original: بدانکه اسم بر دو قسم است: معرفه و نکره. معرفه آنست که موضوع باشد برای چیزی معین، و آن بر هفت نوع است: اول مضمرات، دوم اعلام، چون زَيْدٌ وَعَمْرٌو، سوم اسمای اشارات، چهارم اسمای موصوله، و این دو قسم را مبهمات گویند، پنجم معرفه بندا، چون يَا رَجُلُ، ششم معرف بالف و لام، چون اَلرَّجُلُ،
text.en: Know that the noun is of two divisions: definite (maʿrifa) and indefinite (nakira). The definite is that which is laid down for a particular thing, and it is of seven sorts: first, the pronouns; second, the proper names, as Zaydun and ʿAmrun; third, the demonstratives; fourth, the relative nouns — these two divisions are called the vague nouns (mubhamāt); fifth, what is made definite by calling, as yā rajulu “O man”; sixth, what is made definite by the alif and lām, as al-rajulu “the man”;

text.original: هفتم مضاف بیکی ازینها، چون غُلَامُهُ، وَغُلَامُ زَيْدٍ، وَغُلَامُ هٰذَا، وَغُلَامُ الَّذِي عِنْدِي، وَغُلَامُ الرَّجُلِ. و نکره آنست که موضوع باشد برای چیزی غیر معین، چون رَجُلٌ وَفَرَسٌ.
text.en: seventh, what is muḍāf to one of these, as ghulāmuhu “his servant”, ghulāmu Zaydin “Zayd's servant”, ghulāmu hādhā “this one's servant”, ghulāmu alladhī ʿindī “the servant of the one who is with me” and ghulāmu al-rajuli “the man's servant”. The indefinite is that which is laid down for a thing that is not particular, as rajulun “a man” and farasun “a horse”.

lessons.title: The masculine and the feminine
body: The noun is masculine or feminine. The masculine has no sign of the feminine, rajulun; the feminine has one, imraʾatun. The signs are four: the tāʾ, Ṭalḥatu; the short alif, ḥublā, “pregnant”; the long alif, ḥamrāʾu, “red (f.)”; and the implied tāʾ, as arḍun, “earth”.

The implied tāʾ is the instructive one. Arḍun has no visible sign, yet it is feminine: “in origin it was arḍatun, as is shown by urayḍatun”, its diminutive, “for the diminutive takes nouns back to their origin”. Such a word is called feminine by hearing (muʾannath samāʿī): the Arabs treat it as feminine, and the diminutive shows the tāʾ they mean.

The feminine is also real (ḥaqīqī) or verbal (lafẓī). The real has a male of its kind over against it: imraʾatun against rajulun, nāqatun, “a she-camel”, against jamalun. The verbal has none: ẓulmatun, “darkness”, quwwatun, “strength”, are feminine only in their words.

The difference has a use in the chapter of the verb (lesson 26): with a real feminine doer the verb must take the tāʾ, qāmat Hindun; with a verbal feminine, ṭalaʿa al-shamsu and ṭalaʿati al-shamsu are both said. Ṭalḥa, finally, is a man's name: the tāʾ is a sign in the word, not in the person.

tasks.prompt: How does the diminutive show that arḍun is feminine?
tasks.answer: The diminutive takes a noun back to its origin, and the diminutive of arḍ is urayḍatun, with a tāʾ. So the tāʾ is implied in arḍun.

tasks.prompt: Is quwwatun a real or a verbal feminine? And nāqatun?
tasks.answer: Quwwatun is verbal: there is no male “strength” over against it. Nāqatun is real: it has jamalun, the male camel, over against it.

text.original: بدانکه اسم بر دو صنف است: مذکر و مؤنث. مذکر آنست که در وی علامت تأنیث نباشد، چون رَجُلٌ، و مؤنث آنست که در وی علامت تأنیث باشد، چون اِمْرَأَةٌ. و علامت تأنیث چهار است: تا، چون طَلْحَةُ، و الف مقصوره، چون حُبْلَى، و الف ممدوده، چون حَمْرَاءُ، و تای مقدره، چون أَرْضٌ که در اصل أَرْضَةٌ بوده است، بدلیل أُرَيْضَةٌ، زیرا که تصغیر اسما را باصل خود برد، و این را مؤنث سماعی گویند.
text.en: Know that the noun is of two classes: masculine and feminine. The masculine is that in which there is no sign of the feminine, as rajulun “a man”; the feminine is that in which there is a sign of the feminine, as imraʾatun “a woman”. The signs of the feminine are four: the tāʾ, as Ṭalḥatu Ṭalḥa; the short alif (alif maqṣūra), as ḥublā “pregnant”; the long alif (alif mamdūda), as ḥamrāʾu “red (f.)”; and the implied tāʾ, as arḍun “earth”, which in origin was arḍatun, as is shown by urayḍatun [its diminutive], for the diminutive takes nouns back to their origin; and this is called the feminine by hearing (muʾannath samāʿī).

text.original: بدانکه مؤنث بر دو قسم است: حقیقی و لفظی. حقیقی آنست که بازای او حیوانی مذکر باشد، چون اِمْرَأَةٌ که بازای رَجُلٌ است، و نَاقَةٌ که بازای جَمَلٌ است. و لفظی آنست که بازای او حیوانی مذکر نباشد، چون ظُلْمَةٌ وَقُوَّةٌ.
text.en: Know that the feminine is of two divisions: real (ḥaqīqī) and verbal (lafẓī). The real is that which has a male animal over against it, as imraʾatun “a woman”, which is over against rajulun “a man”, and nāqatun “a she-camel”, which is over against jamalun “a camel”. The verbal is that which has no male animal over against it, as ẓulmatun “darkness” and quwwatun “strength”.

lessons.title: Singular, dual and plural; the broken plural
body: The noun is singular, dual or plural. The singular indicates one, rajulun. The dual indicates two, by an alif, or a yāʾ with a fatḥa before it, and a nūn with a kasra joined to its end: rajulāni, rajulayni.

The plural indicates more than two “because a change has been made in the singular”, in the wording, rijālun from rajulun, or by implication: fulkun, “ships”, has the same letters in the singular and the plural, but the singular fulk is on the pattern of quflun, “lock”, and the plural fulk on the pattern of usdun, “lions”. The change is there, only it is not heard.

By its wording the plural is broken (taksīr) or sound (taṣḥīḥ). The broken plural does not keep the build of the singular sound: rijālun, masājidu. Its patterns in the triliteral “depend on hearing, and analogy has no room in them”: one learns each plural with its singular. But nouns of four and five letters make it on faʿālilu: Jaʿfarun → jaʿāfiru; jaḥmarishun, “old woman”, → jaḥāmiru, “with the fifth letter dropped”.

The sound plural is the next lesson. Note here the reason for the name: in rijāl the singular rajul is “broken” into a new shape, in muslimūna the singular muslim stays whole and only an ending is added.

text.original: بدانکه اسم بر سه صنف است: واحد و مثنی و مجموع. واحد آنست که دلالت کند بر یکی، چون رَجُلٌ. و مثنی آنست که دلالت کند بر دو بسبب آنکه الف یا یای ماقبل مفتوح و نون مکسوره باخرش پیوندد، چون رَجُلَانِ وَرَجُلَيْنِ.
text.en: Know that the noun is of three classes: singular (wāḥid), dual (muthannā) and plural (majmūʿ). The singular is that which indicates one, as rajulun “a man”. The dual is that which indicates two because an alif, or a yāʾ with a fatḥa before it, and a nūn with kasra are joined to its end, as rajulāni and rajulayni “two men”.

text.original: و مجموع آنست که دلالت کند بر بیش از دو بسبب آنکه تغییری در واحد کرده باشند، لَفْظًا چون رِجَالٌ، یا تَقْدِيرًا چون فُلْكٌ، که واحدش نیز فُلْكٌ است بر وزن قُفْلٌ، و جمعش هم فُلْكٌ بر وزن أُسْدٌ.
text.en: The plural is that which indicates more than two because a change has been made in the singular, in the wording, as rijālun “men”, or by implication, as fulkun “ships”, whose singular is also fulk, on the pattern of quflun “lock”, and whose plural is also fulk, on the pattern of usdun “lions”.

text.original: بدانکه جمع باعتبار لفظ بر دو قسم است: جمع تکسیر و جمع تصحیح. جمع تکسیر آنست که بنای واحد در وی سلامت نباشد، چون رِجَالٌ وَمَسَاجِدُ. و ابنیه جمع تکسیر در ثلاثی بسماع تعلق دارد و قیاس را در وی مجالی نیست، اما در رباعی و خماسی بر وزن فَعَالِلُ آید، چون جَعْفَرٌ وَجَعَافِرُ، و جَحْمَرِشٌ وَجَحَامِرُ بحذف حرف خامس.
text.en: Know that the plural, with regard to the wording, is of two divisions: the broken plural (jamʿ taksīr) and the sound plural (jamʿ taṣḥīḥ). The broken plural is that in which the build of the singular is not kept sound, as rijālun “men” and masājidu “mosques”. The patterns of the broken plural in the triliteral depend on hearing, and analogy has no room in them; but in the quadriliteral and the quinqueliteral it comes on the pattern faʿālilu, as Jaʿfarun [a name] and jaʿāfiru, and jaḥmarishun “old woman” and jaḥāmiru, with the fifth letter dropped.

lessons.title: The sound plurals; the plurals of few and of many
body: The sound plural keeps the build of the singular whole. The masculine adds a wāw with a ḍamma before it, or a yāʾ with a kasra before it, and a nūn with a fatḥa: muslimūna, muslimīna. The feminine adds an alif with a tāʾ: muslimātun.

By its meaning the plural is of few (qilla) or of many (kathra). The plural of few is used for fewer than ten, and has four patterns: afʿulun, aklubun, “dogs”; afʿālun, aqwālun, “sayings”; afʿilatun, aʿwinatun, “helpers”; and fiʿlatun, ghilmatun, “boys”; and the two sound plurals without al-, muslimūna and muslimātun. The plural of many is for ten and more, and its patterns are all the others.

So the same thing may have two plurals: a few boys are ghilmatun; many boys, ghilmānun, on a pattern of many. The rule is about the patterns, not about every use: the Qurʾān and the poets often use one for the other, and the books of ṣarf discuss this. Naḥw-i Mīr gives the beginner the rule.
Note “without al-”: with al-, as al-muslimūna, the sound plural takes in all, and so is no longer a plural of few.

text.original: و جمع تصحیح آنست که بنای واحد در وی سلامت ماند، و آن بر دو قسم است: جمع مذکر و جمع مؤنث. جمع مذکر آنست که واوی ماقبل مضموم یا یائی ماقبل مکسور و نونی مفتوح در آخرش پیوندد، چون مُسْلِمُونَ وَمُسْلِمِينَ، و جمع مؤنث آنست که الفی با تائی باخرش پیوندد، چون مُسْلِمَاتٌ.
text.en: The sound plural is that in which the build of the singular remains sound, and it is of two divisions: the masculine plural and the feminine plural. The masculine plural is that to whose end a wāw with a ḍamma before it, or a yāʾ with a kasra before it, and a nūn with fatḥa are joined, as muslimūna and muslimīna “Muslims”; and the feminine plural is that to whose end an alif with a tāʾ is joined, as muslimātun “Muslim women”.

text.original: بدانکه جمع باعتبار معنی بر دو نوع است: جمع قلت و جمع کثرت. جمع قلت آنست که بر کم از ده اطلاق کنند، و آن را چهار بناست: أَفْعُلٌ مثل أَكْلُبٌ، و أَفْعَالٌ چون أَقْوَالٌ، و أَفْعِلَةٌ مثل أَعْوِنَةٌ، و فِعْلَةٌ چون غِلْمَةٌ، و دو جمع تصحیح بی الف و لام، یعنی مُسْلِمُونَ وَمُسْلِمَاتٌ. و جمع کثرت آنست که بر ده و بیشتر از ده اطلاق کنند، و ابنیه آن هر چه غیر ازین شش بناست.
text.en: Know that the plural, with regard to the meaning, is of two sorts: the plural of few (jamʿ qilla) and the plural of many (jamʿ kathra). The plural of few is that which is used for less than ten, and it has four patterns: afʿulun, as aklubun “dogs”; afʿālun, as aqwālun “sayings”; afʿilatun, as aʿwinatun “helpers”; and fiʿlatun, as ghilmatun “boys”; and the two sound plurals without the alif and lām, that is, muslimūna and muslimātun. The plural of many is that which is used for ten and more than ten, and its patterns are all those other than these six patterns.

lessons.title: The iʿrāb of the noun (1): vowels, the feminine plural, the diptote
body: The iʿrāb of the noun is three: rafʿ, naṣb and jarr. By its ways of iʿrāb the firmly placed noun is of sixteen kinds, and the book takes them in turn, each with three sentences: jāʾanī…, raʾaytu…, marartu bi-…, to show the three states.

The first three take the three vowels: the sound singular with tanwīn, Zaydun; the singular that “runs like the sound”, ending in a wāw or yāʾ after a quiescent letter, dalwun, “bucket”; and the broken plural, rijālun: jāʾanī Zaydun wa-dalwun wa-rijālun; raʾaytu Zaydan wa-dalwan wa-rijālan; marartu bi-Zaydin wa-dalwin wa-rijālin.
The fourth is the sound feminine plural: rafʿ with the ḍamma, naṣb and jarr with the kasra: hunna muslimātun; raʾaytu muslimātin; marartu bi-muslimātin. The kasra stands in for the fatḥa in naṣb.

The fifth is the diptote (ghayr munṣarif), “a noun in which there are two of the causes”: rafʿ with the ḍamma, naṣb and jarr with the fatḥa: jāʾa ʿUmaru, raʾaytu ʿUmara, marartu bi-ʿUmara. Here the fatḥa stands in for the kasra. The nine causes are listed here and explained in the conclusion (lesson 37).

text.original: بدانکه اعراب اسم سه است: رفع و نصب و جر، و اسم متمکن باعتبار وجوه اعراب بر شانزده قسم است. اول مفرد منصرف صحیح، چون زَيْدٌ، دوم مفرد منصرف جاری مجرای صحیح، چون دَلْوٌ، سوم جمع مکسر منصرف، چون رِجَالٌ؛ رفع شان بضمه باشد و نصب بفتحه و جر بکسره، چون جَاءَنِي زَيْدٌ وَدَلْوٌ وَرِجَالٌ، وَرَأَيْتُ زَيْدًا وَدَلْوًا وَرِجَالًا، وَمَرَرْتُ بِزَيْدٍ وَدَلْوٍ وَرِجَالٍ.
text.en: Know that the iʿrāb of the noun is three: rafʿ, naṣb and jarr. With regard to the ways of iʿrāb, the mutamakkin noun is of sixteen divisions. First, the sound singular that takes tanwīn, as Zaydun; second, the singular that takes tanwīn and runs like the sound, as dalwun “bucket”; third, the broken plural that takes tanwīn, as rijālun “men”. Their rafʿ is with the ḍamma, their naṣb with the fatḥa and their jarr with the kasra, as jāʾanī Zaydun wa-dalwun wa-rijālun “Zayd, a bucket and men came to me”, wa-raʾaytu Zaydan wa-dalwan wa-rijālan “and I saw Zayd, a bucket and men” and wa-marartu bi-Zaydin wa-dalwin wa-rijālin “and I passed by Zayd, a bucket and men”.

text.original: چهارم جمع مؤنث سالم، رفعش بضمه باشد و نصب و جر بکسره، چون هُنَّ مُسْلِمَاتٌ، وَرَأَيْتُ مُسْلِمَاتٍ، وَمَرَرْتُ بِمُسْلِمَاتٍ.
text.en: Fourth, the sound feminine plural: its rafʿ is with the ḍamma, and its naṣb and jarr with the kasra, as hunna muslimātun “they are Muslim women”, wa-raʾaytu muslimātin “and I saw Muslim women” and wa-marartu bi-muslimātin “and I passed by Muslim women”.

text.original: پنجم غیر منصرف، و آن اسمیست که دو سبب از اسباب منع صرف در وی باشد، و اسباب منع صرف نه است: عدل و وصف و تأنیث و معرفه و عجمه و جمع و ترکیب و وزن فعل و الف و نون زائدتان، چون عُمَرُ وَأَحْمَرُ وَطَلْحَةُ وَزَيْنَبُ وَإِبْرَاهِيمُ وَمَسَاجِدُ وَمَعْدِيكَرِبُ وَأَحْمَدُ وَعِمْرَانُ؛ رفعش بضمه باشد و نصب و جر بفتحه، چون جَاءَ عُمَرُ، وَرَأَيْتُ عُمَرَ، وَمَرَرْتُ بِعُمَرَ.
text.en: Fifth, the diptote (ghayr munṣarif), which is a noun in which there are two of the causes that keep a noun from tanwīn. The causes are nine: deflection (ʿadl), the adjective (waṣf), femininity (taʾnīth), definiteness (maʿrifa), foreignness (ʿujma), the plural (jamʿ), the compound (tarkīb), the pattern of the verb (wazn al-fiʿl), and the added alif and nūn; as ʿUmaru ʿUmar, aḥmaru “red”, Ṭalḥatu Ṭalḥa, Zaynabu Zaynab, Ibrāhīmu Ibrāhīm, masājidu “mosques”, Maʿdīkaribu Maʿdīkarib, Aḥmadu Aḥmad and ʿImrānu ʿImrān. Its rafʿ is with the ḍamma, and its naṣb and jarr with the fatḥa, as jāʾa ʿUmaru “ʿUmar came”, wa-raʾaytu ʿUmara “and I saw ʿUmar” and wa-marartu bi-ʿUmara “and I passed by ʿUmar”.

lessons.title: The iʿrāb of the noun (2): the six nouns, the dual, the plural
body: The sixth kind is the six nouns, “in their full form (mukabbara)”, that is, not as diminutives, “when they are muḍāf to something other than the yāʾ of the speaker”: abun, akhun, ḥamun, hanun, famun and dhū mālin. Their rafʿ is with the wāw, naṣb with the alif, jarr with the yāʾ: jāʾa abūka, raʾaytu abāka, marartu bi-abīka.

The seventh to ninth kinds take the alif in rafʿ and “the yāʾ with a fatḥa before it” in naṣb and jarr: the dual, rajulāni; kilā and kiltā when muḍāf to a pronoun; and ithnāni and ithnatāni: jāʾanī rajulāni wa-kilāhumā wa-thnāni; raʾaytu rajulayni wa-kilayhimā wa-thnayni.

The tenth to twelfth kinds take the wāw with a ḍamma before it in rafʿ, and the yāʾ with a kasra before it in naṣb and jarr: the sound masculine plural, muslimūna; ūlū, “possessors”; and ʿishrūna to tisʿūna: jāʾanī muslimūna wa-ūlū mālin wa-ʿishrūna rajulan; raʾaytu muslimīna wa-ūlī mālin wa-ʿishrīna rajulan.
The book's three-sentence method lets the student see the rule at once. Read the three sentences of each kind aloud, and listen to the letter that changes: wāw, alif, yāʾ; alif, yāʾ; wāw, yāʾ.

terms.en: the six nouns in their full form, not diminutive

text.original: ششم اسمای سته مکبره، وقتیکه مضاف باشند بغیر یای متکلم، چون أَبٌ وَأَخٌ وَحَمٌ وَهَنٌ وَفَمٌ وَذُو مَالٍ؛ رفع شان بواو باشد و نصب بالف و جر بیا، چون جَاءَ أَبُوكَ، وَرَأَيْتُ أَبَاكَ، وَمَرَرْتُ بِأَبِيكَ.
text.en: Sixth, the six nouns in their full form (mukabbara), when they are muḍāf to something other than the yāʾ of the speaker: abun “father”, akhun “brother”, ḥamun “father-in-law”, hanun “thing”, famun “mouth” and dhū mālin “possessor of wealth”. Their rafʿ is with the wāw, their naṣb with the alif and their jarr with the yāʾ, as jāʾa abūka “your father came”, wa-raʾaytu abāka “and I saw your father” and wa-marartu bi-abīka “and I passed by your father”.

text.original: هفتم مثنی، چون رَجُلَانِ، هشتم كِلَا وَكِلْتَا مضاف بمضمر، نهم اِثْنَانِ وَاثْنَتَانِ؛ رفع شان بالف باشد و نصب و جر بیای ماقبل مفتوح، چون جَاءَنِي رَجُلَانِ وَكِلَاهُمَا وَاثْنَانِ، وَرَأَيْتُ رَجُلَيْنِ وَكِلَيْهِمَا وَاثْنَيْنِ، وَمَرَرْتُ بِرَجُلَيْنِ وَكِلَيْهِمَا وَاثْنَيْنِ.
text.en: Seventh, the dual, as rajulāni “two men”; eighth, kilā and kiltā “both” muḍāf to a pronoun; ninth, ithnāni and ithnatāni “two”. Their rafʿ is with the alif, and their naṣb and jarr with the yāʾ with a fatḥa before it, as jāʾanī rajulāni wa-kilāhumā wa-ithnāni “two men came to me, both of them, two”, wa-raʾaytu rajulayni wa-kilayhimā wa-ithnayni “and I saw two men, both of them, two” and wa-marartu bi-rajulayni wa-kilayhimā wa-ithnayni “and I passed by two men, both of them, two”.

text.original: دهم جمع مذکر سالم، چون مُسْلِمُونَ، یازدهم أُولُو، دوازدهم عِشْرُونَ تا تِسْعُونَ؛ رفع شان بواو ماقبل مضموم باشد و نصب و جر بیای ماقبل مکسور، چون جَاءَنِي مُسْلِمُونَ وَأُولُو مَالٍ وَعِشْرُونَ رَجُلًا، وَرَأَيْتُ مُسْلِمِينَ وَأُولِي مَالٍ وَعِشْرِينَ رَجُلًا، وَمَرَرْتُ بِمُسْلِمِينَ وَأُولِي مَالٍ وَعِشْرِينَ رَجُلًا.
text.en: Tenth, the sound masculine plural, as muslimūna “Muslims”; eleventh, ūlū “possessors”; twelfth, ʿishrūna “twenty” up to tisʿūna “ninety”. Their rafʿ is with the wāw with a ḍamma before it, and their naṣb and jarr with the yāʾ with a kasra before it, as jāʾanī muslimūna wa-ūlū mālin wa-ʿishrūna rajulan “Muslims, possessors of wealth and twenty men came to me”, wa-raʾaytu muslimīna wa-ūlī mālin wa-ʿishrīna rajulan “and I saw Muslims, possessors of wealth and twenty men” and wa-marartu bi-muslimīna wa-ūlī mālin wa-ʿishrīna rajulan “and I passed by Muslims, possessors of wealth and twenty men”.

lessons.title: The iʿrāb of the noun (3): the implied iʿrāb
body: The last four kinds show their iʿrāb only in part, or not at all. The thirteenth is the maqṣūr, whose end is a short alif, Mūsā; the fourteenth is a noun muḍāf to the yāʾ of the speaker that is not a sound masculine plural, ghulāmī. Both have every state implied: jāʾanī Mūsā wa-ghulāmī, raʾaytu Mūsā wa-ghulāmī, marartu bi-Mūsā wa-ghulāmī, “in the wording they are always the same”.

The fifteenth is the manqūṣ, whose end is a yāʾ with a kasra before it, al-qāḍī: rafʿ with an implied ḍamma, naṣb with an audible fatḥa, jarr with an implied kasra: jāʾa al-qāḍī, raʾaytu al-qāḍiya, marartu bi-l-qāḍī.

The sixteenth is the sound masculine plural muḍāf to the yāʾ of the speaker, muslimiyya, “my Muslims”. In rafʿ its wāw is implied; in naṣb and jarr it has the yāʾ: hāʾulāʾi muslimiyya, raʾaytu muslimiyya, marartu bi-muslimiyya. The book shows how the rafʿ came about: muslimūna joined to -ya lost its nūn by the iḍāfa (muslimūya); the wāw and the yāʾ met, the first quiescent, so the wāw became a yāʾ and merged into it, and the ḍamma before it became a kasra: muslimiyya.
So in all three states the word is muslimiyya; only the analysis differs. This kind of reasoning, a form explained by the changes of ṣarf, is where naḥw rests on the ṣarf the student learnt first.

tasks.prompt: Explain how muslimūna + yāʾ of the speaker becomes muslimiyya.

text.original: سیزدهم اسم مقصور، و آن اسمیست که آخرش الف مقصوره باشد، چون مُوسَى، چهاردهم غیر جمع مذکر سالم مضاف بیای متکلم، چون غُلَامِي؛ رفع شان بتقدیر ضمه باشد و نصب بتقدیر فتحه و جر بتقدیر کسره، و در لفظ همیشه یکسان باشند، چون جَاءَنِي مُوسَى وَغُلَامِي، وَرَأَيْتُ مُوسَى وَغُلَامِي، وَمَرَرْتُ بِمُوسَى وَغُلَامِي.
text.en: Thirteenth, the maqṣūr noun, which is a noun whose end is a short alif, as Mūsā Mūsā; fourteenth, what is not a sound masculine plural, muḍāf to the yāʾ of the speaker, as ghulāmī “my servant”. Their rafʿ is with an implied ḍamma, their naṣb with an implied fatḥa and their jarr with an implied kasra, and in the wording they are always the same, as jāʾanī Mūsā wa-ghulāmī “Mūsā and my servant came to me”, wa-raʾaytu Mūsā wa-ghulāmī “and I saw Mūsā and my servant” and wa-marartu bi-Mūsā wa-ghulāmī “and I passed by Mūsā and my servant”.

text.original: پانزدهم اسم منقوص، و آن اسمیست که آخرش یائی ماقبل مکسور باشد، چون اَلْقَاضِي؛ رفعش بتقدیر ضمه باشد و نصب بفتحه لفظی و جرش بتقدیر کسره، چون جَاءَ الْقَاضِي، وَرَأَيْتُ الْقَاضِيَ، وَمَرَرْتُ بِالْقَاضِي.
text.en: Fifteenth, the manqūṣ noun, which is a noun whose end is a yāʾ with a kasra before it, as al-qāḍī “the judge”. Its rafʿ is with an implied ḍamma, its naṣb with an audible fatḥa and its jarr with an implied kasra, as jāʾa al-qāḍī “the judge came”, wa-raʾaytu al-qāḍiya “and I saw the judge” and wa-marartu bi-al-qāḍī “and I passed by the judge”.

text.original: شانزدهم جمع مذکر سالم مضاف بیای متکلم، چون مُسْلِمِيَّ؛ رفعش بتقدیر واو باشد و نصب و جرش بیای ماقبل مکسور، چون هٰؤُلَاءِ مُسْلِمِيَّ، که در اصل مُسْلِمُونَ بود، نون باضافت ساقط شد، واو و یا جمع شده بودند و سابق ساکن بود، واو را بیا بدل کردند و یا را در یا ادغام کردند، مُسْلِمِيَّ شد، و ضمه میم را بکسره بدل کردند، وَرَأَيْتُ مُسْلِمِيَّ، وَمَرَرْتُ بِمُسْلِمِيَّ.
text.en: Sixteenth, the sound masculine plural muḍāf to the yāʾ of the speaker, as muslimiyya “my Muslims”. Its rafʿ is with an implied wāw, and its naṣb and jarr with the yāʾ with a kasra before it, as hāʾulāʾi muslimiyya “these are my Muslims”, which in origin was muslimūna: the nūn fell away through the iḍāfa; the wāw and the yāʾ had come together and the first was unvowelled, so the wāw was changed into yāʾ and the yāʾ assimilated into the yāʾ, and it became muslimiyya; and the ḍamma of the mīm was changed into a kasra; and wa-raʾaytu muslimiyya “and I saw my Muslims” and wa-marartu bi-muslimiyya “and I passed by my Muslims”.

lessons.title: The iʿrāb of the muḍāriʿ in four kinds
body: The iʿrāb of the muḍāriʿ is three: rafʿ, naṣb and jazm, and by its ways the muḍāriʿ is of four kinds. The first is the sound verb without a visible pronoun of the dual, the masculine plural or the woman addressed: rafʿ with the ḍamma, naṣb with the fatḥa, jazm with the sukūn: huwa yaḍribu, lan yaḍriba, lam yaḍrib.

The second is the singular whose last letter is a wāw or a yāʾ, yaghzū, yarmī: rafʿ with an implied ḍamma, naṣb with an audible fatḥa, jazm by dropping the lām: huwa yaghzū wa-yarmī; lan yaghzuwa wa-lan yarmiya; lam yaghzu wa-lam yarmi. The third is the singular ending in an alif, yarḍā: rafʿ and naṣb implied, jazm by dropping the lām: huwa yarḍā, lan yarḍā, lam yarḍa.

The fourth is the verb, sound or weak, with the pronouns of the dual, the masculine plural and the woman addressed: rafʿ by keeping the nūn, yaḍribāni, yaghzuwāni, yarmiyāni, yarḍayāni; yaḍribūna, yaghzūna, yarmūna, yarḍawna; taḍribīna, taghzīna, tarmīna, tarḍayna; naṣb and jazm by dropping it: lan yaḍribā, lam yaghzuwā, lan yarmū, lam tarḍay.

The book sets the sound verb beside three weak ones in every line, so that the student sees the one rule under the changing forms. The weak forms here are from the print: the weak verb's own changes are the business of the ṣarf books.

tasks.prompt: Why are lan yarḍā and huwa yarḍā the same in wording?

text.original: بدانکه اعراب مضارع سه است: رفع و نصب و جزم، و فعل مضارع باعتبار وجوه اعراب بر چهار قسم است. اول صحیح مجرد از ضمیر بارز مرفوع برای تثنیه و جمع مذکر و برای واحد مؤنث مخاطبه؛ رفعش بضمه باشد و نصب بفتحه و جزم بسکون، چون هُوَ يَضْرِبُ، وَلَنْ يَضْرِبَ، وَلَمْ يَضْرِبْ.
text.en: Know that the iʿrāb of the muḍāriʿ is three: rafʿ, naṣb and jazm. With regard to the ways of iʿrāb, the muḍāriʿ verb is of four divisions. First, the sound [verb] free of a visible pronoun in rafʿ for the dual and the masculine plural and for the singular feminine addressed: its rafʿ is with the ḍamma, its naṣb with the fatḥa and its jazm with the sukūn, as huwa yaḍribu “he hits”, wa-lan yaḍriba “and he will not hit” and wa-lam yaḍrib “and he did not hit”.

text.original: دوم مفرد معتل واوی، چون يَغْزُو، و یائی، چون يَرْمِي؛ رفعش بتقدیر ضمه باشد و نصب بفتحه لفظی و جزم بحذف لام، چون هُوَ يَغْزُو وَيَرْمِي، وَلَنْ يَغْزُوَ وَلَنْ يَرْمِيَ، وَلَمْ يَغْزُ وَلَمْ يَرْمِ. سوم مفرد معتل الفی، چون يَرْضَى؛ رفعش بتقدیر ضمه باشد و نصب بتقدیر فتحه و جزم بحذف لام، چون هُوَ يَرْضَى، وَلَنْ يَرْضَى، وَلَمْ يَرْضَ.
text.en: Second, the singular weak with wāw, as yaghzū “he raids”, and with yāʾ, as yarmī “he throws”: its rafʿ is with an implied ḍamma, its naṣb with an audible fatḥa and its jazm by dropping the lām, as huwa yaghzū wa-yarmī “he raids and throws”, wa-lan yaghzuwa wa-lan yarmiya “and he will not raid and will not throw” and wa-lam yaghzu wa-lam yarmi “and he did not raid and did not throw”. Third, the singular weak with alif, as yarḍā “he is pleased”: its rafʿ is with an implied ḍamma, its naṣb with an implied fatḥa and its jazm by dropping the lām, as huwa yarḍā “he is pleased”, wa-lan yarḍā “and he will not be pleased” and wa-lam yarḍa “and he was not pleased”.

text.original: چهارم صحیح یا معتل با ضمایر و نونهای مذکوره؛ رفع شان باثبات نون باشد، چنانکه در تثنیه گوئی: هُمَا يَضْرِبَانِ وَيَغْزُوَانِ وَيَرْمِيَانِ وَيَرْضَيَانِ، و در جمع مذکر گوئی: هُمْ يَضْرِبُونَ وَيَغْزُونَ وَيَرْمُونَ وَيَرْضَوْنَ، و در مفرد مؤنث حاضر گوئی: أَنْتِ تَضْرِبِينَ وَتَغْزِينَ وَتَرْمِينَ وَتَرْضَيْنَ؛
text.en: Fourth, the sound or the weak with the pronouns and the nūns mentioned: their rafʿ is by keeping the nūn, as you say in the dual humā yaḍribāni wa-yaghzuwāni wa-yarmiyāni wa-yarḍayāni “they two hit, raid, throw and are pleased”, in the masculine plural hum yaḍribūna wa-yaghzūna wa-yarmūna wa-yarḍawna “they hit, raid, throw and are pleased”, and in the singular feminine present anti taḍribīna wa-taghzīna wa-tarmīna wa-tarḍayna “you (f.) hit, raid, throw and are pleased”;

text.original: و نصب و جزم بحذف نون، چنانکه در تثنیه گوئی: لَنْ يَضْرِبَا، وَلَنْ يَغْزُوَا، وَلَنْ يَرْمِيَا، وَلَنْ يَرْضَيَا، وَلَمْ يَضْرِبَا، وَلَمْ يَغْزُوَا، وَلَمْ يَرْمِيَا، وَلَمْ يَرْضَيَا، و در جمع مذکر گوئی: لَنْ يَضْرِبُوا، وَلَنْ يَغْزُوا، وَلَنْ يَرْمُوا، وَلَنْ يَرْضَوْا، وَلَمْ يَضْرِبُوا، وَلَمْ يَغْزُوا، وَلَمْ يَرْمُوا، وَلَمْ يَرْضَوْا،
text.en: and their naṣb and jazm are by dropping the nūn, as you say in the dual lan yaḍribā, wa-lan yaghzuwā, wa-lan yarmiyā, wa-lan yarḍayā “they two will not hit, raid, throw, be pleased” and wa-lam yaḍribā, wa-lam yaghzuwā, wa-lam yarmiyā, wa-lam yarḍayā “they two did not hit, raid, throw, were not pleased”; and in the masculine plural lan yaḍribū, wa-lan yaghzū, wa-lan yarmū, wa-lan yarḍaw “they will not hit, raid, throw, be pleased” and wa-lam yaḍribū, wa-lam yaghzū, wa-lam yarmū, wa-lam yarḍaw “they did not hit, raid, throw, were not pleased”;

text.original: و در واحد مؤنث حاضر گوئی: لَنْ تَضْرِبِي، وَلَنْ تَغْزِي، وَلَنْ تَرْمِي، وَلَنْ تَرْضَيْ، وَلَمْ تَضْرِبِي، وَلَمْ تَغْزِي، وَلَمْ تَرْمِي، وَلَمْ تَرْضَيْ.
text.en: and in the singular feminine present you say lan taḍribī, wa-lan taghzī, wa-lan tarmī, wa-lan tarḍay “you (f.) will not hit, raid, throw, be pleased” and wa-lam taḍribī, wa-lam taghzī, wa-lam tarmī, wa-lam tarḍay “you (f.) did not hit, raid, throw, were not pleased”.

lessons.title: The governors; the particles of jarr, inna and its sisters, mā and lā
body: Now the governors (ʿawāmil) of iʿrāb. They are verbal (lafẓī) or abstract (maʿnawī), and the verbal are of three kinds, particles, verbs and nouns, “which we shall set out in three chapters”. Chapter one, on the particles, has two sections: those that govern the noun, in five kinds, and those that govern the muḍāriʿ.

The first kind is the particles of jarr, seventeen: bā, min, ilā, ḥattā, fī, the lām, rubba, the wāw and the tāʾ of oath, ʿan, ʿalā, the kāf of likening, mudh, mundhu, and ḥāshā, khalā, ʿadā. They put the noun after them in jarr: al-mālu li-Zaydin, “the wealth belongs to Zayd”. These are the seventeen that al-Jurjānī's al-ʿAwāmil al-miʾa lists too.

The second kind is the six particles that resemble the verb: inna, anna, kaʾanna, lākinna, layta and laʿalla. They put the ism in naṣb and the khabar in rafʿ: inna Zaydan qāʾimun, “Zayd is standing”, “Zayd the ism of inna and qāʾim the khabar of inna”. Their meanings: inna and anna confirm (taḥqīq), kaʾanna likens, lākinna corrects (istidrāk), layta wishes, laʿalla hopes.

The third kind is mā and lā that resemble laysa: they do the work of laysa, the ism in rafʿ and the khabar in naṣb: mā Zaydun qāʾiman, “Zayd is not standing”. Inna and mā are mirror images: with inna the first noun is in naṣb, with mā the second.

text.original: بدانکه عوامل اعراب دو قسمت است: لفظی و معنوی. لفظی بر سه قسمت است: حروف و افعال و اسما، و این را در سه باب بیان کنیم ان شاء الله تعالی.
text.en: Know that the governors of iʿrāb are of two divisions: verbal (lafẓī) and abstract (maʿnawī). The verbal are of three divisions, particles, verbs and nouns, and we shall set them out in three chapters, God Most High willing.

text.original: فصل اول: در حروف عامله در اسم، و آن پنج قسم است. قسم اول حروف جر، و آن هفده است: بَا، وَمِنْ، وَإِلَى، وَحَتَّى، وَفِي، وَلَامْ، وَرُبَّ، وَوَاوِ قسم، وَتَاءِ قسم، وَعَنْ، وَعَلَى، وَكَافِ تشبیه، وَمُذْ، وَمُنْذُ، وَحَاشَا، وَخَلَا، وَعَدَا. این حروف در اسم روند و آخرش را جر کنند، چون اَلْمَالُ لِزَيْدٍ.
text.en: Section one: on the particles that govern the noun; they are of five divisions. The first division: the particles of jarr, which are seventeen: bā [the bāʾ] “with”, min “from”, ilā “to”, ḥattā “until”, fī “in”, the lām “for”, rubba “many a”, the wāw of oath, the tāʾ of oath, ʿan “away from”, ʿalā “on”, the kāf of likening, mudh and mundhu “since”, and ḥāshā, khalā and ʿadā “except”. These particles go on the noun and put its end in jarr, as al-mālu li-Zaydin “the wealth belongs to Zayd”.

text.original: دوم حروف مشبهه بفعل، و آن شش است: إِنَّ، وَأَنَّ، وَكَأَنَّ، وَلٰكِنَّ، وَلَيْتَ، وَلَعَلَّ. این حروف اسم را نصب کنند و خبر را رفع، چون إِنَّ زَيْدًا قَائِمٌ، زید اسم إِنَّ است و قائم خبر إِنَّ. بدانکه إِنَّ و أَنَّ حروف تحقیق است، و كَأَنَّ حرف تشبیه، و لٰكِنَّ حرف استدراک، و لَيْتَ حرف تمنی، و لَعَلَّ حرف ترجی.
text.en: Second, the particles that resemble the verb (ḥurūf mushabbaha bi-l-fiʿl), which are six: inna, anna, kaʾanna, lākinna, layta and laʿalla. These particles put the ism in naṣb and the khabar in rafʿ, as inna Zaydan qāʾimun “Zayd is standing”: Zayd is the ism of inna and qāʾim the khabar of inna. Know that inna and anna are particles of confirming (taḥqīq), kaʾanna a particle of likening (tashbīh), lākinna a particle of correcting (istidrāk), layta a particle of wishing (tamannī) and laʿalla a particle of hoping (tarajjī).

text.original: سوم مَا و لَا الْمُشَبَّهَتَانِ بِلَيْسَ، و این هر دو عمل لَيْسَ کنند، چنانکه گوئی: مَا زَيْدٌ قَائِمًا، زید اسم ما است و قائما خبر او.
text.en: Third, the mā and lā that resemble laysa (mā wa-lā al-mushabbahatān bi-laysa). Both of them do the work of laysa, as you say mā Zaydun qāʾiman “Zayd is not standing”: Zayd is the ism of mā and qāʾiman its khabar.

lessons.title: The lā that denies the kind; the particles of calling
body: The fourth kind is the lā that denies the whole kind. Its ism “is mostly muḍāf and in naṣb, and its khabar in rafʿ”: lā ghulāma rajulin ẓarīfun fī al-dāri, “no man's servant is witty in the house”. If its ism is a single indefinite, it is fixed on the fatḥa: lā rajula fī al-dāri, “there is no man in the house”.

If a definite follows lā, lā does not govern, the definite is a mubtadaʾ in rafʿ, and lā must be repeated with another definite: lā Zaydun ʿindī wa-lā ʿAmrun, “neither Zayd nor ʿAmr is with me”. And if a single indefinite follows it, repeated with another, five ways are allowed: lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata; lā ḥawlun wa-lā quwwatun; lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwatun; lā ḥawlun wa-lā quwwata; lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwatan illā bi-llāh.

The fifth kind is the five particles of calling: yā, ayā, hayā, ay and the hamza. They put in naṣb a munādā that is muḍāf, yā ʿAbda Allāhi; one like a muḍāf, yā ṭāliʿan jabalan, “O you climbing a mountain”; and an indefinite not particular, the blind man's yā rajulan khudh bi-yadī, “O [some] man, take my hand!”.

The single definite munādā is fixed on its sign of rafʿ: yā Zaydu, yā Zaydāni, yā muslimūna, yā Mūsā, yā qāḍī. And “ay and the hamza are for one who is near, ayā and hayā for one who is far, and yā is for both”.

text.original: چهارم لای نفی جنس، اسم این لا اکثر مضاف باشد، منصوب، و خبرش مرفوع، چون لَا غُلَامَ رَجُلٍ ظَرِيفٌ فِي الدَّارِ، و اگر نکره مفرد باشد مبنی باشد بر فتحه، چون لَا رَجُلَ فِي الدَّارِ، و اگر بعد لا معرفه باشد تکرار لا با معرفه دیگر لازم باشد، و لا ملغی باشد، یعنی عمل نکند، و آن معرفه مرفوع باشد بابتدا، چون لَا زَيْدٌ عِنْدِي وَلَا عَمْرٌو،
text.en: Fourth, the lā that denies the whole kind. The ism of this lā is mostly muḍāf and in naṣb, and its khabar in rafʿ, as lā ghulāma rajulin ẓarīfun fī al-dāri “no man's servant is witty in the house”. If it is a single indefinite, it is mabnī on the fatḥa, as lā rajula fī al-dāri “there is no man in the house”. If after lā there is a definite, repeating lā with another definite is necessary, and lā is cancelled, that is, it does not govern, and that definite is marfūʿ as mubtadaʾ, as lā Zaydun ʿindī wa-lā ʿAmrun “neither Zayd nor ʿAmr is with me”;

text.original: و اگر بعد آن لا نکره مفرد باشد مکرر با نکره دیگر، درو پنج وجه روا است، چون لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ، وَلَا حَوْلٌ وَلَا قُوَّةٌ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ، وَلَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةٌ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ، وَلَا حَوْلٌ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ، وَلَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةً إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ.
text.en: and if after that lā there is a single indefinite, repeated with another indefinite, five ways are allowed in it, as lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-Allāhi, lā ḥawlun wa-lā quwwatun illā bi-Allāhi, lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwatun illā bi-Allāhi, lā ḥawlun wa-lā quwwata illā bi-Allāhi and lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwatan illā bi-Allāhi “there is no might and no power except through God”.

text.original: پنجم حروف ندا، و آن پنج است: يَا، وَأَيَا، وَهَيَا، وَأَيْ، و همزه مفتوحه. و این حروف منادای مضاف را نصب کنند، چون يَا عَبْدَ اللَّهِ، و مشابه بمضاف را، چون يَا طَالِعًا جَبَلًا، و نکره غیر معین را، چنانکه اعمی گوید: يَا رَجُلًا خُذْ بِيَدِي.
text.en: Fifth, the particles of calling (ḥurūf al-nidāʾ), which are five: yā, ayā, hayā, ay and the hamza with fatḥa. These particles put in naṣb a munādā that is muḍāf, as yā ʿAbda Allāhi “O ʿAbd Allāh”; one that resembles a muḍāf, as yā ṭāliʿan jabalan “O you climbing a mountain”; and an indefinite that is not particular, as the blind man says: yā rajulan khudh bi-yadī “O [some] man, take my hand!”.

text.original: و منادای مفرد معرفه مبنی باشد بر علامت رفع، چون يَا زَيْدُ، وَيَا زَيْدَانِ، وَيَا مُسْلِمُونَ، وَيَا مُوسَى، وَيَا قَاضِي. بدانکه أَيْ و همزه برای نزدیک است، و أَيَا و هَيَا برای دور، و يَا عام است.
text.en: The single definite munādā is mabnī on the sign of rafʿ, as yā Zaydu “O Zayd”, yā Zaydāni “O two Zayds”, yā muslimūna “O Muslims”, yā Mūsā “O Mūsā” and yā qāḍī “O judge”. Know that ay and the hamza are for one who is near, ayā and hayā for one who is far, and yā is for both.

lessons.title: The particles of naṣb of the muḍāriʿ; an unseen
body: Section two of the chapter: the particles that govern the muḍāriʿ, in two kinds. The first puts it in naṣb, and has four. An: urīdu an taqūma, “I want you to stand”: “an with the verb has the sense of a maṣdar, that is, urīdu qiyāmaka, ‘I want your standing’, and for this reason it is called maṣdariyya”. Lan: lan yakhruja Zaydun, “Zayd will not go out”, “for emphasizing the negation”.

Kay: aslamtu kay adkhula al-jannata, “I became Muslim so that I may enter Paradise”. Idhan: idhan ukrimaka, “then I will honour you”, said in answer to one who says anā ātīka ghadan, “I will come to you tomorrow”.

An is also hidden after six particles and still puts the verb in naṣb: ḥattā, marartu ḥattā adkhula al-balada, “I went on until I should enter the town”; the lām of denial, mā kāna Allāhu li-yuʿadhdhibahum (Q 8:33); aw in the sense of “until” or “unless”, la-alzamannaka aw tuʿṭiyanī ḥaqqī, “I will stick to you until you give me my due”; the wāw of turning (wāw al-ṣarf); the lām of kay; and the fāʾ in answer to six things, command, prohibition, negation, question, wish and offer. “Their examples are well known”, says the book, and leaves them to the teacher.

The wāw of turning is the wāw that turns the verb away from the rule of what came before it, as in lā taʾkuli al-samaka wa-tashraba al-labana: the commentators give it as the wāw that means “with”. The fāʾ in answer is the fāʾ of cause, after which the verb is in naṣb.

text.original: فصل دوم: در حروف عامله در فعل مضارع، و آن بر دو قسم است. قسم اول حروفیکه فعل مضارع را نصب کنند، و آن چهار است: اول أَنْ، چون أُرِيدُ أَنْ تَقُومَ، و أَنْ با فعل بمعنی مصدر باشد، یعنی أُرِيدُ قِيَامَكَ، و بدین سبب او را مصدریه گویند. دوم لَنْ، چون لَنْ يَخْرُجَ زَيْدٌ، و لَنْ برای تأکید نفی است.
text.en: Section two: on the particles that govern the muḍāriʿ verb; they are of two divisions. The first division: the particles that put the muḍāriʿ verb in naṣb, which are four. First, an, as urīdu an taqūma “I want you to stand”; an with the verb has the sense of a maṣdar, that is, urīdu qiyāmaka “I want your standing”, and for this reason it is called maṣdariyya. Second, lan, as lan yakhruja Zaydun “Zayd will not go out”; lan is for emphasizing the negation.

text.original: سوم كَيْ، چون أَسْلَمْتُ كَيْ أَدْخُلَ الْجَنَّةَ. چهارم إِذَنْ، چون إِذَنْ أُكْرِمَكَ در جواب کسی که گوید: أَنَا آتِيكَ غَدًا.
text.en: Third, kay, as aslamtu kay adkhula al-jannata “I became Muslim so that I may enter Paradise”. Fourth, idhan, as idhan ukrimaka “then I will honour you”, in answer to one who says anā ātīka ghadan “I will come to you tomorrow”.

text.original: و بدانکه أَنْ بعد از شش حروف مقدر باشد و فعل مضارع را نصب کند: حَتَّى، نحو: مَرَرْتُ حَتَّى أَدْخُلَ الْبَلَدَ، و لام جحد، نحو: مَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيُعَذِّبَهُمْ، و أَوْ بمعنی إِلَى أَنْ یا إِلَّا أَنْ، نحو: لَأَلْزَمَنَّكَ أَوْ تُعْطِيَنِي حَقِّي، و واو الصرف، و لام كَيْ، و فا که در جواب شش چیز است: امر و نهی و نفی و استفهام و تمنی و عرض، وَأَمْثِلَتُهَا مَشْهُورَةٌ.
text.en: Know that an is implied after six particles and puts the muḍāriʿ verb in naṣb: ḥattā, as marartu ḥattā adkhula al-balada “I went on until I should enter the town”; the lām of denial (lām al-jaḥd), as mā kāna Allāhu li-yuʿadhdhibahum “God would not punish them” [8:33]; aw in the sense of ilā an “until” or illā an “unless”, as la-alzamannaka aw tuʿṭiyanī ḥaqqī “I will stick to you until you give me my due”; the wāw of turning (wāw al-ṣarf); the lām of kay; and the fāʾ that is in answer to six things: command, prohibition, negation, question, wish and offer. Their examples are well known.

lessons.title: The particles of jazm; the condition and its requital
body: The second kind puts the muḍāriʿ in jazm, five particles: lam, lammā, the lām of command, the lā of prohibition, and the in of condition: lam yanṣur, “he did not help”; lammā yanṣur, “he has not yet helped”; li-yanṣur, “let him help”; lā tanṣur, “do not help!”; in tanṣur anṣur, “if you help, I will help”.

In goes on two sentences: in taḍrib aḍrib, “if you hit, I will hit”; the first is called the condition (sharṭ), the second the requital (jazāʾ). “In is for the future, even if it goes on a past”: in ḍarabta ḍarabtu means “if you hit, I will hit”. There “the jazm is implied, because the past is not muʿrab”: the past verb keeps its form and is in jazm only in its place.

When the requital is a nominal sentence, a command, a prohibition or a prayer, it must take the fāʾ: in taʾtinī fa-anta mukramun, “if you come to me, you are honoured”; in raʾayta Zaydan fa-akrimhu, “if you see Zayd, honour him”; in atāka ʿAmrun fa-lā tuhinhu, “if ʿAmr comes to you, do not humiliate him”; in akramtanī fa-jazāka Allāhu khayran, “if you honour me, may God reward you with good”.
The last example teaches something: jazāka Allāhu khayran is a past verb in form, but a prayer in meaning, so it needs the fāʾ. It is the meaning of the requital, not only its form, that decides.
