text.original: قسم دوم حروفیکه فعل مضارع را جزم کنند، و آن پنج است: لَمْ، وَلَمَّا، و لام امر، و لای نهی، و إِنْ شرطیه، چون لَمْ يَنْصُرْ، وَلَمَّا يَنْصُرْ، وَلِيَنْصُرْ، وَلَا تَنْصُرْ، وَإِنْ تَنْصُرْ أَنْصُرْ.
text.en: The second division: the particles that put the muḍāriʿ verb in jazm, which are five: lam, lammā, the lām of command, the lā of prohibition and the conditional in, as lam yanṣur “he did not help”, lammā yanṣur “he has not yet helped”, li-yanṣur “let him help”, lā tanṣur “do not help!” and in tanṣur anṣur “if you help, I will help”.

text.original: بدانکه إِنْ در دو جمله رود، چون إِنْ تَضْرِبْ أَضْرِبْ، جمله اول را شرط گویند و جمله دوم را جزا، و إِنْ برای مستقبل است اگرچه در ماضی رود، چون إِنْ ضَرَبْتَ ضَرَبْتُ، و اینجا جزم تقدیری بود، زیرا که ماضی معرب نیست.
text.en: Know that in goes on two sentences, as in taḍrib aḍrib “if you hit, I will hit”: the first sentence is called the condition (sharṭ) and the second sentence the requital (jazāʾ). In is for the future, even if it goes on a past, as in ḍarabta ḍarabtu “if you hit, I will hit”; and here the jazm is implied, because the past is not muʿrab.

text.original: و بدانکه چون جزای شرط جمله اسمیه باشد یا امر یا نهی یا دعا، فا در جزا آوردن لازم بود، چنانکه گوئی: إِنْ تَأْتِنِي فَأَنْتَ مُكْرَمٌ، وَإِنْ رَأَيْتَ زَيْدًا فَأَكْرِمْهُ، وَإِنْ أَتَاكَ عَمْرٌو فَلَا تُهِنْهُ، وَإِنْ أَكْرَمْتَنِي فَجَزَاكَ اللَّهُ خَيْرًا.
text.en: Know that when the requital of the condition is a nominal sentence, or a command, a prohibition or a prayer, bringing the fāʾ into the requital is necessary, as you say in taʾtinī fa-anta mukramun “if you come to me, you are honoured”, wa-in raʾayta Zaydan fa-akrimhu “and if you see Zayd, honour him”, wa-in atāka ʿAmrun fa-lā tuhinhu “and if ʿAmr comes to you, do not humiliate him” and wa-in akramtanī fa-jazāka Allāhu khayran “and if you honour me, may God reward you with good”.

parts.title: Chapter two: the governing of verbs

lessons.title: Chapter two: the verb and what it puts in rafʿ and naṣb
body: “No verb is without governing.” The active verb, intransitive or transitive, puts the fāʿil in rafʿ: qāma Zaydun, “Zayd stood”, ḍaraba ʿAmrun, “ʿAmr hit”. And it puts six nouns in naṣb, every verb alike.

They are: the mafʿūl muṭlaq, qāma Zaydun qiyāman, ḍaraba Zaydun ḍarban; the mafʿūl fīhi, ṣumtu yawma al-jumuʿati, jalastu ʿindaka; the mafʿūl maʿahu, jāʾa al-bardu wa-l-jubbāti, “the cold came with the cloaks”; the mafʿūl lahu, qumtu ikrāman li-Zaydin, ḍarabtuhu taʾdīban, “I beat him to teach him manners”; the ḥāl, jāʾa Zaydun rākiban, “Zayd came riding”; and the tamyīz, when the doer's share in the verb is vague, ṭāba Zaydun nafsan, “Zayd was pleased in soul”.

The transitive verb has one more: the mafʿūl bihi, ḍaraba Zaydun ʿAmran, “Zayd hit ʿAmr”. “The intransitive verb does not have this governing.” So an intransitive verb governs seven, a transitive verb eight.

Notice that the six do not need a transitive verb: one can stand a standing, stand on Friday, stand out of respect, stand riding. That is why the book lists them first, for every verb, and the mafʿūl bihi after, for some.

text.original: بدانکه هیچ فعل غیر عامل نیست، و افعال در عمل بر دو گونه است. قسم اول معروف. بدانکه فعل معروف، خواه لازم باشد خواه متعدی، فاعل را رفع کند، چون قَامَ زَيْدٌ، وَضَرَبَ عَمْرٌو، و شش اسم را نصب کند:
text.en: Know that no verb is without governing, and verbs are of two kinds in their governing. The first division: the active. Know that the active verb, whether intransitive or transitive, puts the fāʿil in rafʿ, as qāma Zaydun “Zayd stood” and ḍaraba ʿAmrun “ʿAmr hit”, and puts six nouns in naṣb:

text.original: اول مفعول مطلق را، چون قَامَ زَيْدٌ قِيَامًا، وَضَرَبَ زَيْدٌ ضَرْبًا، دوم مفعول فیه را، چون صُمْتُ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ، وَجَلَسْتُ عِنْدَكَ، سوم مفعول معه را، چون جَاءَ الْبَرْدُ وَالْجُبَّاتِ، أَيْ مَعَ الْجُبَّاتِ، چهارم مفعول له را، چون قُمْتُ إِكْرَامًا لِزَيْدٍ، وَضَرَبْتُهُ تَأْدِيبًا، پنجم حال را، چون جَاءَ زَيْدٌ رَاكِبًا، ششم تمییز را، وقتیکه در نسبت فعل بفاعل ابهامی باشد، چون طَابَ زَيْدٌ نَفْسًا.
text.en: first, the mafʿūl muṭlaq, as qāma Zaydun qiyāman “Zayd stood a standing” and ḍaraba Zaydun ḍarban “Zayd hit a hitting”; second, the mafʿūl fīhi, as ṣumtu yawma al-jumuʿati “I fasted on Friday” and jalastu ʿindaka “I sat with you”; third, the mafʿūl maʿahu, as jāʾa al-bardu wa-al-jubbāti “the cold came with the cloaks”, ay maʿa al-jubbāti “that is, together with the cloaks”; fourth, the mafʿūl lahu, as qumtu ikrāman li-Zaydin “I stood out of respect for Zayd” and ḍarabtuhu taʾdīban “I beat him to teach him manners”; fifth, the ḥāl, as jāʾa Zaydun rākiban “Zayd came riding”; sixth, the tamyīz, when there is a vagueness in the attribution of the verb to the fāʿil, as ṭāba Zaydun nafsan “Zayd was pleased in soul”.

text.original: اما فعل متعدی مفعول به را نصب کند، چون ضَرَبَ زَيْدٌ عَمْرًا، و این عمل فعل لازم را نباشد.
text.en: As for the transitive verb, it puts the mafʿūl bihi in naṣb, as ḍaraba Zaydun ʿAmran “Zayd hit ʿAmr”; and the intransitive verb does not have this governing.

lessons.title: The fāʿil, the mafʿūl muṭlaq, fīhi, maʿahu and lahu defined
body: Now each is defined. The fāʿil is “a noun before which there is a verb attributed to that noun in the way of the verb's subsisting in that noun”: Zayd in ḍaraba Zaydun. Three points: it is a noun; the verb comes before it; and the act is said of it as of the one in whom it subsists, the hitting is in Zayd as its doer, not as its object.
The mafʿūl muṭlaq is “a maṣdar that comes after a verb, that maṣdar having the meaning of that verb”: ḍarban in ḍarabtu ḍarban, qiyāman in qumtu qiyāman.

The mafʿūl fīhi is “a noun in which the verb mentioned takes place”, called the adverb (ẓarf): of time, yawma in ṣumtu yawma al-jumuʿati; or of place, ʿinda in jalastu ʿindaka. The mafʿūl maʿahu is “a noun mentioned after a wāw in the sense of maʿa”: al-jubbāti in jāʾa al-bardu wa-l-jubbāti, that is, maʿa al-jubbāti.

The mafʿūl lahu is “a noun that indicates a thing that is the cause of the verb mentioned”: ikrāman in qumtu ikrāman li-Zaydin, “I stood out of respect for Zayd”. Each name tells the question it answers: muṭlaq, “what act?”; fīhi, “when, where?”; maʿahu, “with what?”; lahu, “why?”.

tasks.answer: It is a noun (Zayd); a verb comes before it (ḍaraba); and the verb is said of it as subsisting in it (the hitting is Zayd's act). So Zayd is the fāʿil.

text.original: فصل: بدانکه فاعل اسمیست که پیش ازوی فعلی باشد مسند بدان اسم بر طریق قیام فعل بدان اسم، چون زید در ضَرَبَ زَيْدٌ. و مفعول مطلق مصدریست که واقع شود بعد از فعلی، و آن مصدر بمعنی آن فعل باشد، چون ضَرْبًا در ضَرَبْتُ ضَرْبًا، و قِيَامًا در قُمْتُ قِيَامًا.
text.en: Section. Know that the fāʿil is a noun before which there is a verb attributed to that noun in the way of the verb's subsisting in that noun, as Zayd in ḍaraba Zaydun “Zayd hit”. The mafʿūl muṭlaq is a maṣdar that comes after a verb, that maṣdar having the meaning of that verb, as ḍarban in ḍarabtu ḍarban “I hit a hitting”, and qiyāman in qumtu qiyāman “I stood a standing”.

text.original: و مفعول فیه اسمیست که فعل مذکور دروی واقع شود، و او را ظرف گویند، و ظرف بر دو گونه است: ظرف زمان، چون يَوْمَ در صُمْتُ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ، و ظرف مکان، چون عِنْدَ در جَلَسْتُ عِنْدَكَ. و مفعول معه اسمیست که مذکور شود بعد از واو بمعنی مع، چون وَالْجُبَّاتِ در جَاءَ الْبَرْدُ وَالْجُبَّاتِ، أَيْ مَعَ الْجُبَّاتِ.
text.en: The mafʿūl fīhi is a noun in which the verb mentioned takes place; it is called the adverb (ẓarf). The ẓarf is of two kinds: the adverb of time, as yawma in ṣumtu yawma al-jumuʿati “I fasted on Friday”, and the adverb of place, as ʿinda in jalastu ʿindaka “I sat with you”. The mafʿūl maʿahu is a noun that is mentioned after a wāw in the sense of maʿa “with”, as wa-al-jubbāti in jāʾa al-bardu wa-al-jubbāti “the cold came with the cloaks”, ay maʿa al-jubbāti “that is, together with the cloaks”.

text.original: و مفعول له اسمیست که دلالت کند بر چیزی که سبب فعل مذکور باشد، چون إِكْرَامًا در قُمْتُ إِكْرَامًا لِزَيْدٍ.
text.en: The mafʿūl lahu is a noun that indicates a thing that is the cause of the verb mentioned, as ikrāman in qumtu ikrāman li-Zaydin “I stood out of respect for Zayd”.

lessons.title: The ḥāl, the tamyīz and the mafʿūl bihi defined
body: The ḥāl is “an indefinite noun that indicates the state” of the fāʿil, rākiban in jāʾa Zaydun rākiban; or of the mafʿūl, mashdūdan in ḍarabtu Zaydan mashdūdan, “I beat Zayd bound”; or of both, rākibayni in laqītu Zaydan rākibayni, “I met Zayd, both of us riding”. The one whose state it is, the dhū al-ḥāl, is mostly definite; if it is indefinite, the ḥāl comes first: jāʾanī rākiban rajulun, “a man came to me riding”. The ḥāl may also be a sentence: raʾaytu al-amīra wa-huwa rākibun, “I saw the emir while he was riding”.

The tamyīz is “a noun that removes vagueness” from a number, ʿindī aḥada ʿashara dirhaman, “I have eleven dirhams”; a weight, ʿindī riṭlun zaytan, “I have a raṭl of oil”; a measure, ʿindī qafīzāni burran, “two qafīzs of wheat”; or an area, mā fī al-samāʾi qadru rāḥatin saḥāban, “there is not in the sky so much as a palm's breadth of cloud”.
The mafʿūl bihi is “a noun on which the act of the fāʿil falls”: ʿAmran in ḍaraba Zaydun ʿAmran.

Then a principle: “all these manṣūb nouns come after the sentence is complete, and the sentence is complete with the verb and the fāʿil; for this reason it is said: al-manṣūbu faḍlatun, ‘the manṣūb is an extra’.” The pillars of the sentence are in rafʿ; what is in naṣb adds to a sentence already whole.

text.original: و حال اسمیست نکره که دلالت کند بر هیئت فاعل، چون رَاكِبًا در جَاءَ زَيْدٌ رَاكِبًا، یا بر هیئت مفعول، چون مَشْدُودًا در ضَرَبْتُ زَيْدًا مَشْدُودًا، یا بر هیئت هر دو، چون رَاكِبَيْنِ در لَقِيتُ زَيْدًا رَاكِبَيْنِ، و فاعل و مفعول را ذو الحال گویند، و آن غَالِبًا معرفه باشد، و اگر نکره باشد حال را مقدم دارند، چون جَاءَنِي رَاكِبًا رَجُلٌ، و حال جمله نیز باشد، چنانچه رَأَيْتُ الْأَمِيرَ وَهُوَ رَاكِبٌ.
text.en: The ḥāl is an indefinite noun that indicates the state of the fāʿil, as rākiban in jāʾa Zaydun rākiban “Zayd came riding”; or the state of the mafʿūl, as mashdūdan in ḍarabtu Zaydan mashdūdan “I beat Zayd bound”; or the state of both, as rākibayni in laqītu Zaydan rākibayni “I met Zayd, both of us riding”. The fāʿil and the mafʿūl are called the owner of the ḥāl (dhū al-ḥāl); it is mostly definite, and if it is indefinite the ḥāl is put first, as jāʾanī rākiban rajulun “a man came to me riding”. The ḥāl may also be a sentence, as raʾaytu al-amīra wa-huwa rākibun “I saw the emir while he was riding”.

text.original: و تمییز اسمیست که رفع ابهام کند از عدد، چون عِنْدِي أَحَدَ عَشَرَ دِرْهَمًا، یا از وزن، چون عِنْدِي رِطْلٌ زَيْتًا، یا از کیل، چون عِنْدِي قَفِيزَانِ بُرًّا، یا از مساحت، چون مَا فِي السَّمَاءِ قَدْرُ رَاحَةٍ سَحَابًا.
text.en: The tamyīz is a noun that removes vagueness from a number, as ʿindī aḥada ʿashara dirhaman “I have eleven dirhams”; or from a weight, as ʿindī riṭlun zaytan “I have a raṭl of oil”; or from a measure of capacity, as ʿindī qafīzāni burran “I have two qafīzs of wheat”; or from an area, as mā fī al-samāʾi qadru rāḥatin saḥāban “there is not in the sky [so much as] the size of a palm in clouds”.

text.original: و مفعول به اسمیست که فعل فاعل برو واقع شود، چون ضَرَبَ زَيْدٌ عَمْرًا. بدانکه این همه منصوبات بعد از تمامی جمله باشند، و جمله بفعل و فاعل تمام شود، و بدین سبب گویند که اَلْمَنْصُوبُ فَضْلَةٌ.
text.en: The mafʿūl bihi is a noun on which the act of the fāʿil falls, as ḍaraba Zaydun ʿAmran “Zayd hit ʿAmr”. Know that all these manṣūb nouns come after the sentence is complete, and the sentence is complete with the verb and the fāʿil; for this reason it is said: al-manṣūbu faḍlatun “the manṣūb is an extra”.

lessons.title: The fāʿil, explicit and pronoun; the passive verb
body: The fāʿil is explicit (muẓhar), ḍaraba Zaydun, or a pronoun (muḍmar), visible, ḍarabtu, or hidden: in Zaydun ḍaraba, “Zayd, he hit”, the fāʿil of ḍaraba is huwa, hidden in it, and Zaydun is a mubtadaʾ.

When the fāʿil is a real feminine, or a feminine pronoun, the verb must take the tāʾ: qāmat Hindun; Hindun qāmat, “that is, she”. With an explicit noun that is not really feminine, and with an explicit broken plural, both ways are allowed: ṭalaʿa al-shamsu and ṭalaʿati al-shamsu, “the sun rose”; qāla al-rijālu and qālati al-rijālu, “the men said”.

The second division of the verb is the passive. It “puts the mafʿūl bihi in rafʿ in the place of the fāʿil, and puts the rest in naṣb”. The book's sentence shows them all at once: ḍuriba Zaydun yawma al-jumuʿati amāma al-amīri ḍarban shadīdan fī dārihi taʾdīban wa-l-khashabata, “Zayd was beaten on Friday before the emir, a hard beating, in his house, to teach him manners, with the stick”: Zaydun in rafʿ, and the ẓarf of time, the ẓarf of place, the muṭlaq, the lahu and the maʿahu in naṣb.

The passive is called “the verb whose doer is not named” (fiʿl mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu), and its marfūʿ “the object whose doer is not named” (mafʿūl mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu), the Indian books' name for what others call the deputy of the doer.

text.original: فصل: بدانکه فاعل بر دو قسمت است: مظهر، چون ضَرَبَ زَيْدٌ، و مضمر، بارز چون ضَرَبْتُ، و مستتر، یعنی پوشیده، چون زَيْدٌ ضَرَبَ، که فاعل ضَرَبَ هُوَ است در ضَرَبَ مستتر. بدانکه چون فاعل مؤنث حقیقی باشد یا ضمیر مؤنث، علامت تأنیث در فعل لازم باشد، چون قَامَتْ هِنْدٌ، وَهِنْدٌ قَامَتْ، أَيْ هِيَ، و در مظهر مؤنث غیر حقیقی و در مظهر جمع تکسیر دو وجه روا باشد، چون طَلَعَ الشَّمْسُ وَطَلَعَتِ الشَّمْسُ، وَقَالَ الرِّجَالُ وَقَالَتِ الرِّجَالُ.
text.en: Section. Know that the fāʿil is of two divisions: explicit (muẓhar), as ḍaraba Zaydun “Zayd hit”; and a pronoun (muḍmar), either visible (bāriz), as ḍarabtu “I hit”, or hidden (mustatir), that is, concealed, as Zaydun ḍaraba “Zayd, he hit”, where the fāʿil of ḍaraba is huwa “he”, hidden in ḍaraba. Know that when the fāʿil is a real feminine or a feminine pronoun, the sign of the feminine in the verb is necessary, as qāmat Hindun “Hind stood” and Hindun qāmat “Hind, she stood”, ay hiya “that is, she”; and with an explicit noun that is not really feminine, and with an explicit broken plural, both ways are allowed, as ṭalaʿa al-shamsu and ṭalaʿati al-shamsu “the sun rose”, and qāla al-rijālu and qālati al-rijālu “the men said”.

text.original: قسم دوم مجهول. بدانکه فعل مجهول بجای فاعل مفعول به را رفع کند، و باقی را نصب، چون ضُرِبَ زَيْدٌ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ أَمَامَ الْأَمِيرِ ضَرْبًا شَدِيدًا فِي دَارِهِ تَأْدِيبًا وَالْخَشَبَةَ، و فعل مجهول را فعل ما لم یسم فاعله گویند، و مرفوعش را مفعول ما لم یسم فاعله گویند.
text.en: The second division: the passive. Know that the passive verb puts the mafʿūl bihi in rafʿ in the place of the fāʿil, and puts the rest in naṣb, as ḍuriba Zaydun yawma al-jumuʿati amāma al-amīri ḍarban shadīdan fī dārihi taʾdīban wa-al-khashabata “Zayd was beaten on Friday before the emir, a hard beating, in his house, to teach him manners, with the stick”. The passive verb is called the verb whose doer is not named (fiʿl mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu), and its marfūʿ is called the object whose doer is not named (mafʿūl mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu).

lessons.title: The four kinds of transitive verb
body: The transitive verb is of four kinds. To one object: ḍaraba Zaydun ʿAmran. To two objects where one may keep to one: aʿṭā, “gave”, and verbs of its meaning: aʿṭaytu Zaydan dirhaman, “I gave Zayd a dirham”, and aʿṭaytu Zaydan alone is also correct.

To two objects where one may not keep to one: the verbs of the heart, ʿalimtu, ẓanantu, ḥasibtu, khiltu, zaʿamtu, raʾaytu and wajadtu: ʿalimtu Zaydan fāḍilan, “I knew Zayd to be excellent”; ẓanantu Zaydan ʿāliman. “I knew Zayd” would not say what was known of him. And to three objects: aʿlama, arā, anbaʾa, akhbara, khabbara, nabbaʾa and ḥaddatha: aʿlama Allāhu Zaydan ʿAmran fāḍilan, “God made Zayd know ʿAmr to be excellent”.

“All these objects are mafʿūl bihi.” In the passive, any of them may take the doer's place except four: the second object in the chapter of ʿalimtu, the third in the chapter of aʿlamtu, the mafʿūl lahu and the mafʿūl maʿahu. In the chapter of aʿṭaytu the first object is the more fitting: uʿṭiya Zaydun dirhaman, “Zayd was given a dirham”.

The pattern is easy to see: the verbs of three objects are the verbs of the heart made causative, aʿlama from ʿalima, arā from raʾā. “To know Zayd excellent” becomes “to make someone know Zayd excellent”, and one more object is added.

the verbs of the heart: two objects, neither left out
transitive to three objects: aʿlama, arā and others

tasks.answer: With aʿṭā each object is a thing on its own: Zayd was given something, even if it is not named. With ʿalimtu the two objects are one judgement, “Zayd is excellent”; leaving out the second leaves no judgement.

text.original: فصل: بدانکه فعل متعدی بر چهار قسمت است: اول متعدی بیک مفعول، چون ضَرَبَ زَيْدٌ عَمْرًا. دوم متعدی بدو مفعول که اقتصار بر یک مفعول روا باشد، چون أَعْطَى و آنچه در معنی او باشد، چون أَعْطَيْتُ زَيْدًا دِرْهَمًا، و اینجا أَعْطَيْتُ زَيْدًا نیز جائز است.
text.en: Section. Know that the transitive verb is of four divisions. First, transitive to one object, as ḍaraba Zaydun ʿAmran “Zayd hit ʿAmr”. Second, transitive to two objects, where it is allowed to keep to one object, as aʿṭā “he gave” and what is of its meaning, as aʿṭaytu Zaydan dirhaman “I gave Zayd a dirham”; and here aʿṭaytu Zaydan “I gave Zayd” is also allowed.

text.original: سوم متعدی بدو مفعول که اقتصار بر یک مفعول روا نباشد، و این افعال قلوب است، چون عَلِمْتُ وَظَنَنْتُ وَحَسِبْتُ وَخِلْتُ وَزَعَمْتُ وَرَأَيْتُ وَوَجَدْتُ، چون عَلِمْتُ زَيْدًا فَاضِلًا، وَظَنَنْتُ زَيْدًا عَالِمًا. چهارم متعدی بسه مفعول، چون أَعْلَمَ وَأَرَى وَأَنْبَأَ وَأَخْبَرَ وَخَبَّرَ وَنَبَّأَ وَحَدَّثَ، چون أَعْلَمَ اللَّهُ زَيْدًا عَمْرًا فَاضِلًا.
text.en: Third, transitive to two objects, where it is not allowed to keep to one object; these are the verbs of the heart (afʿāl al-qulūb), as ʿalimtu “I knew”, ẓanantu “I supposed”, ḥasibtu “I reckoned”, khiltu “I fancied”, zaʿamtu “I claimed”, raʾaytu “I held” and wajadtu “I found”, as ʿalimtu Zaydan fāḍilan “I knew Zayd to be excellent” and ẓanantu Zaydan ʿāliman “I supposed Zayd to be learned”. Fourth, transitive to three objects, as aʿlama “he made know”, arā “he showed”, anbaʾa, akhbara, khabbara, nabbaʾa and ḥaddatha “he told”, as aʿlama Allāhu Zaydan ʿAmran fāḍilan “God made Zayd know ʿAmr to be excellent”.

text.original: بدانکه این همه مفعولات مفعول به اند. و مفعول دوم در باب عَلِمْتُ و مفعول سوم در باب أَعْلَمْتُ و مفعول له و مفعول معه را بجای فاعل نتوانند نهاد، و دیگرها را شاید، و در باب أَعْطَيْتُ مفعول اول بمفعول ما لم یسم فاعله لائق تر باشد از مفعول دوم.
text.en: Know that all these objects are mafʿūl bihi. The second object in the chapter of ʿalimtu, the third object in the chapter of aʿlamtu, the mafʿūl lahu and the mafʿūl maʿahu cannot be put in the place of the fāʿil, and the others may. In the chapter of aʿṭaytu the first object is more fitting to be the mafʿūl mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu than the second.

lessons.title: The incomplete verbs, and the verbs of approach
body: The incomplete verbs are seventeen in this book: kāna, ṣāra, ẓalla, bāta, aṣbaḥa, aḍḥā, amsā, ʿāda, āḍa, ghadā, rāḥa, mā zāla, mā infakka, mā bariḥa, mā fatiʾa, mā dāma and laysa. Four more than in al-Jurjānī's list: ʿāda, āḍa, ghadā and rāḥa, which here mean “became”, like ṣāra. They “are not complete with the fāʿil alone and need a khabar; for this reason they are called incomplete”.

They go on a nominal sentence, put the musnad ilayhi in rafʿ and the musnad in naṣb: kāna Zaydun qāʾiman: “the marfūʿ is called the ism of kāna and the manṣūb the khabar of kāna; judge the rest by this”. Some of them are in some uses complete: kāna maṭarun, “there was rain”, that is, it came about; this is the complete kāna. And kāna may also be added (zāʾida).

The verbs of nearness (muqāraba) are four: ʿasā, kāda, karaba and awshaka. Like kāna they put the ism in rafʿ and the khabar in naṣb, “except that their khabar is a muḍāriʿ verb with an”, ʿasā Zaydun an yakhruja, “or without an”, ʿasā Zaydun yakhruju.

And with ʿasā a second way: the muḍāriʿ with an may be the fāʿil of ʿasā, and no khabar is needed: ʿasā an yakhruja Zaydun, “it may be that Zayd goes out”, where an yakhruja is in the place of rafʿ, in the sense of a maṣdar: “Zayd's going out may be”.

text.original: فصل: بدانکه افعال ناقصه هفده اند: كَانَ، وَصَارَ، وَظَلَّ، وَبَاتَ، وَأَصْبَحَ، وَأَضْحَى، وَأَمْسَى، وَعَادَ، وَآضَ، وَغَدَا، وَرَاحَ، وَمَا زَالَ، وَمَا انْفَكَّ، وَمَا بَرِحَ، وَمَا فَتِئَ، وَمَا دَامَ، وَلَيْسَ. این افعال بفاعل تنها تمام نشوند و محتاج باشند بخبری، بدین سبب اینها را ناقصه گویند،
text.en: Section. Know that the incomplete verbs (afʿāl nāqiṣa) are seventeen: kāna “was”, ṣāra “became”, ẓalla “was all day”, bāta “was all night”, aṣbaḥa “became in the morning”, aḍḥā “became in the forenoon”, amsā “became in the evening”, ʿāda, āḍa, ghadā and rāḥa “became”, mā zāla, mā infakka, mā bariḥa and mā fatiʾa “did not cease”, mā dāma “as long as” and laysa “is not”. These verbs are not complete with the fāʿil alone and need a khabar; for this reason they are called incomplete;

text.original: و در جمله اسمیه شوند، مسند الیه را رفع کنند و مسند را نصب، چون كَانَ زَيْدٌ قَائِمًا، مرفوع را اسم كَانَ گویند و منصوب را خبر كَانَ، باقی را برین قیاس کن. بدانکه بعضی ازین افعال در بعضی احوال بفاعل تنها تمام شوند، چون كَانَ مَطَرٌ، شد باران، یعنی حاصل شد، و او را كَانَ تامه گویند، و كَانَ زائده نیز باشد.
text.en: and they go on the nominal sentence, put the musnad ilayhi in rafʿ and the musnad in naṣb, as kāna Zaydun qāʾiman “Zayd was standing”: the marfūʿ is called the ism of kāna and the manṣūb the khabar of kāna; judge the rest by this. Know that some of these verbs are in some states complete with the fāʿil alone, as kāna maṭarun “there was rain”, that is, it came about; this is called the complete kāna (kāna tāmma); and kāna may also be added (zāʾida).

text.original: فصل: بدانکه افعال مقاربه چهار است: عَسَى، وَكَادَ، وَكَرَبَ، وَأَوْشَكَ. این افعال در جمله اسمیه شوند، چون كَانَ اسم را رفع کنند و خبر را نصب، الا آنکه خبر اینها فعل مضارع باشد با أَنْ، چون عَسَى زَيْدٌ أَنْ يَخْرُجَ، یا بی أَنْ، چون عَسَى زَيْدٌ يَخْرُجُ، و شاید که فعل مضارع با أَنْ فاعل عَسَى باشد و احتیاج بخبر نیفتد، چون عَسَى أَنْ يَخْرُجَ زَيْدٌ، در محل رفع بمعنی مصدر.
text.en: Section. Know that the verbs of nearness (afʿāl al-muqāraba) are four: ʿasā “it may be that”, kāda “was about to”, karaba “was near to” and awshaka “was on the point of”. These verbs go on the nominal sentence and, like kāna, put the ism in rafʿ and the khabar in naṣb, except that their khabar is a muḍāriʿ verb with an, as ʿasā Zaydun an yakhruja “it may be that Zayd goes out”, or without an, as ʿasā Zaydun yakhruju. The muḍāriʿ verb with an may be the fāʿil of ʿasā, with no need of a khabar, as ʿasā an yakhruja Zaydun “it may be that Zayd goes out”, in the place of rafʿ, in the sense of a maṣdar.

lessons.title: The verbs of praise and blame; the verbs of wonder
body: The verbs of praise are niʿma and ḥabbadhā, of blame biʾsa and sāʾa. What comes after the fāʿil is “the one singled out for praise or for blame”. The fāʿil is of three kinds: made definite by the lām, niʿma al-rajulu Zaydun; muḍāf to what has the lām, niʿma ṣāḥibu al-qawmi Zaydun, “how good a companion of the people is Zayd”; or a hidden pronoun specified by an indefinite in naṣb, niʿma rajulan Zaydun, where the fāʿil is huwa and rajulan its tamyīz, “because huwa is vague”.
Ḥabbadhā Zaydun, “how fine is Zayd”: ḥabba is the verb of praise, dhā its fāʿil, Zaydun the one singled out. And likewise biʾsa al-rajulu Zaydun, sāʾa al-rajulu ʿAmrun.

The verbs of wonder are two forms, made from any maṣdar of the bare triliteral. Mā afʿalahu: mā aḥsana Zaydan, “how fine Zayd is!”, implied ayyu shayʾin aḥsana Zaydan, “what thing has made Zayd fine?”: mā is in the sense of ayyu shayʾin, a mubtadaʾ in the place of rafʿ; aḥsana is the khabar, in the place of rafʿ; its fāʿil is huwa hidden in it; Zaydan is the mafʿūl bihi.

Afʿil bihi: aḥsin bi-Zaydin, “how fine Zayd is!”: aḥsin is “the form of the imperative with the sense of a statement”, implied aḥsana Zaydun, “Zayd became fine”, ṣāra dhā ḥusnin, “came to have beauty”; and the bāʾ is added. So the imperative here commands nothing; Zayd is its fāʿil, with a bāʾ.

text.original: فصل: بدانکه افعال مدح و ذم چهار است: نِعْمَ وَحَبَّذَا برای مدح، وَبِئْسَ وَسَاءَ برای ذم، و هر چه مابعد فاعل باشد آن را مخصوص بالمدح یا مخصوص بالذم گویند، و شرط آنست که فاعل معرف بلام باشد، چون نِعْمَ الرَّجُلُ زَيْدٌ، یا مضاف بسوی معرف بلام، چون نِعْمَ صَاحِبُ الْقَوْمِ زَيْدٌ، یا ضمیر مستتر ممیز بنکره منصوبه، چون نِعْمَ رَجُلًا زَيْدٌ، فاعل نِعْمَ هُوَ است مستتر در نِعْمَ، و رَجُلًا منصوب است بر تمییز، زیرا که هُوَ مبهم است،
text.en: Section. Know that the verbs of praise and blame are four: niʿma “how good” and ḥabbadhā “how fine” for praise, and biʾsa “how bad” and sāʾa “how evil” for blame. Whatever comes after the fāʿil is called the one singled out for praise or for blame (makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ, makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm). The condition is that the fāʿil is made definite by the lām, as niʿma al-rajulu Zaydun “how good a man is Zayd”; or muḍāf to what is made definite by the lām, as niʿma ṣāḥibu al-qawmi Zaydun “how good a companion of the people is Zayd”; or a hidden pronoun specified by an indefinite in naṣb, as niʿma rajulan Zaydun “how good a man is Zayd”: the fāʿil of niʿma is huwa, hidden in niʿma, and rajulan is manṣūb as tamyīz, because huwa is vague;

text.original: و حَبَّذَا زَيْدٌ، حَبَّ فعل مدح است، و ذَا فاعل او، و زَيْدٌ مخصوص بالمدح، و همچنین بِئْسَ الرَّجُلُ زَيْدٌ، وَسَاءَ الرَّجُلُ عَمْرٌو.
text.en: and ḥabbadhā Zaydun “how fine is Zayd”: ḥabba is the verb of praise, dhā its fāʿil and Zaydun the one singled out for praise; and likewise biʾsa al-rajulu Zaydun “how bad a man is Zayd” and wa-sāʾa al-rajulu ʿAmrun “and how evil a man is ʿAmr”.

text.original: فصل: بدانکه افعال تعجب دو صیغه است، از هر مصدر ثلاثی مجرد باشد. اول مَا أَفْعَلَهُ، چون مَا أَحْسَنَ زَيْدًا، چه نیکوست زید، تقدیرش أَيُّ شَيْءٍ أَحْسَنَ زَيْدًا؛ مَا بمعنی أَيُّ شَيْءٍ است در محل رفع بابتدا، و أَحْسَنَ در محل رفع خبر مبتدا، و فاعل أَحْسَنَ هُوَ است درو مستتر، و زَيْدًا مفعول به.
text.en: Section. Know that the verbs of wonder are two forms, [made] from every maṣdar of the bare triliteral. First, mā afʿalahu, as mā aḥsana Zaydan “how fine Zayd is!”; its implied [wording] is ayyu shayʾin aḥsana Zaydan “what thing has made Zayd fine?”: mā is in the sense of ayyu shayʾin, in the place of rafʿ as mubtadaʾ; aḥsana is in the place of rafʿ as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the fāʿil of aḥsana is huwa, hidden in it; and Zaydan is the mafʿūl bihi.

text.original: دوم أَفْعِلْ بِهِ، چون أَحْسِنْ بِزَيْدٍ، أَحْسِنْ صیغه امر است بمعنی خبر، تقدیرش أَحْسَنَ زَيْدٌ، أَيْ صَارَ ذَا حُسْنٍ، و با زائده است.
text.en: Second, afʿil bi-hi, as aḥsin bi-Zaydin “how fine Zayd is!”: aḥsin is the form of the imperative with the sense of a statement; its implied [wording] is aḥsana Zaydun “Zayd became fine”, ay ṣāra dhā ḥusnin “that is, he came to have beauty”; and the bāʾ is added.

lessons.title: Chapter three: the nouns of condition and the nouns of verbs
body: The third chapter is the nouns that govern, in eleven kinds. The first is the nouns of condition “in the sense of in”, nine: man, mā, ayna, matā, ayyun, annā, idhmā, ḥaythumā and mahmā. They put the muḍāriʿ in jazm, the condition and its requital, as in did: man taḍrib aḍrib, “whomever you hit, I will hit”; mā tafʿal afʿal; ayna tajlis ajlis; matā taqum aqum; ayya shayʾin taʾkul ākul, “whatever thing you eat, I will eat”.

The book's examples go on: annā taktub aktub, “wherever you write, I will write”; idhmā tusāfir usāfir, “if ever you travel, I will travel”; ḥaythumā taqṣid aqṣid; mahmā taqʿud aqʿud. Note ayya shayʾin: ayyun is declinable, and here it is in naṣb as the object of taʾkul.

The second and third kinds are the nouns of verbs, which govern as their verb does. Those in the sense of the past, hayhāta, shattāna and sarʿāna, put a noun in rafʿ “as fāʿil”: hayhāta Zaydun, “that is, baʿuda, Zayd is far”. Those in the sense of the imperative to the one present, ruwayda, balha, ḥayyahal, ʿalayka, dūnaka and hā, put a noun in naṣb “as object”: ruwayda Zaydan, “that is, amhilhu, give him time”.
The book explains each noun of a verb by its verb, baʿuda, amhil, and that is the whole rule: the noun of a verb governs what its verb would govern, the past a doer, the transitive command an object.

text.original: و آن یازده قسم است. اول اسمای شرطیه بمعنی إِنْ، و آن نه است: مَنْ، وَمَا، وَأَيْنَ، وَمَتَى، وَأَيٌّ، وَأَنَّى، وَإِذْمَا، وَحَيْثُمَا، وَمَهْمَا، فعل مضارع را جزم کنند، چون مَنْ تَضْرِبْ أَضْرِبْ، وَمَا تَفْعَلْ أَفْعَلْ، وَأَيْنَ تَجْلِسْ أَجْلِسْ، وَمَتَى تَقُمْ أَقُمْ، وَأَيَّ شَيْءٍ تَأْكُلْ آكُلْ، وَأَنَّى تَكْتُبْ أَكْتُبْ، وَإِذْمَا تُسَافِرْ أُسَافِرْ، وَحَيْثُمَا تَقْصِدْ أَقْصِدْ، وَمَهْمَا تَقْعُدْ أَقْعُدْ.
text.en: They are of eleven divisions. First, the conditional nouns in the sense of in, which are nine: man “whoever”, mā “whatever”, ayna “wherever”, matā “whenever”, ayyun “whichever”, annā “wherever”, idhmā “if ever”, ḥaythumā “wherever” and mahmā “whatever”. They put the muḍāriʿ verb in jazm, as man taḍrib aḍrib “whomever you hit, I will hit”, mā tafʿal afʿal “whatever you do, I will do”, ayna tajlis ajlis “wherever you sit, I will sit”, matā taqum aqum “whenever you stand, I will stand”, ayya shayʾin taʾkul ākul “whatever thing you eat, I will eat”, annā taktub aktub “wherever you write, I will write”, idhmā tusāfir usāfir “if ever you travel, I will travel”, ḥaythumā taqṣid aqṣid “wherever you head for, I will head for” and mahmā taqʿud aqʿud “whenever you sit down, I will sit down”.

text.original: دوم اسمای افعال بمعنی ماضی، چون هَيْهَاتَ وَشَتَّانَ وَسَرْعَانَ، اسم را بنا بر فاعلیت رفع کنند، چون هَيْهَاتَ
text.en: Second, the verbal nouns in the sense of the past, as hayhāta “it is far”, shattāna “how different!” and sarʿāna “how quick!”. They put a noun in rafʿ as fāʿil, as hayhāta

text.original: زَيْدٌ، أَيْ بَعُدَ. سوم اسمای افعال بمعنی امر حاضر، چون رُوَيْدَ وَبَلْهَ وَحَيَّهَلْ وَعَلَيْكَ وَدُونَكَ وَهَا، اسم را نصب کنند بنا بر مفعولیت، چون رُوَيْدَ زَيْدًا، أَيْ أَمْهِلْهُ.
text.en: Zaydun “Zayd is far”, ay baʿuda “that is, he is far”. Third, the verbal nouns in the sense of the imperative to the one present, as ruwayda “give respite!”, balha “leave aside!”, ḥayyahal “come quickly!”, ʿalayka “keep to!”, dūnaka “take!” and hā “take!”. They put a noun in naṣb as mafʿūl, as ruwayda Zaydan “give Zayd respite”, ay amhilhu “that is, grant him delay”.

lessons.title: The active participle, the passive participle, the resembling adjective
lessons.arabic: اسْمُ الْفَاعِلِ وَاسْمُ الْمَفْعُولِ وَالصِّفَةُ الْمُشَبَّهَةُ
lessons.transliteration: ism al-fāʿil wa-ism al-mafʿūl wa-l-ṣifa al-mushabbaha
body: The fourth kind is the active participle, which “in the sense of the present or the future does the work of the active verb, on condition that it leans on a word before it”. The book names six such words. A mubtadaʾ: Zaydun qāʾimun abūhu, Zaydun ḍāribun abūhu ʿAmran. A described noun: marartu bi-rajulin ḍāribin abūhu Bakran. A relative: jāʾanī al-qāʾimu abūhu, jāʾanī al-ḍāribu abūhu ʿAmran.

An owner of a ḥāl: jāʾanī Zaydun rākiban ghulāmuhu farasan, “Zayd came to me, his servant riding a horse”. The hamza of question: a-ḍāribun Zaydun ʿAmran, “is Zayd hitting ʿAmr?”. A particle of negation: mā qāʾimun Zaydun, “Zayd is not standing”. “And the same work that qāma and ḍaraba did, qāʾim and ḍārib do”: rafʿ of a doer, and naṣb of an object if the verb is transitive.

The fifth is the passive participle, which in the sense of the present or the future does the work of the passive verb, on the same condition: Zaydun maḍrūbun abūhu; ʿAmrun muʿṭan ghulāmuhu dirhaman, “ʿAmr, his servant is given a dirham”; Bakrun maʿlūmun ibnuhu fāḍilan; Khālidun mukhbarun ibnuhu ʿAmran fāḍilan. Maḍrūb, muʿṭan, maʿlūm and mukhbar do what ḍuriba, uʿṭiya, ʿulima and ukhbira did: one, two or three objects, the first in rafʿ.

The sixth is the resembling adjective (al-ṣifa al-mushabbaha), which does the work of its verb on the same condition: Zaydun ḥasanun ghulāmuhu, “Zayd, his servant is handsome”: “the same work that ḥasuna did, ḥasan does”. The book's rule is in each case one sentence long: the noun works as the verb it comes from.

text.original: چهارم اسم فاعل بمعنی حال یا استقبال عمل فعل معروف کند، بشرط آنکه اعتماد کرده باشد بر لفظی که پیش ازو باشد، و آن لفظ یا مبتدا باشد، چون زَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ أَبُوهُ، و در متعدی چون زَيْدٌ ضَارِبٌ أَبُوهُ عَمْرًا، یا موصوف، چون مَرَرْتُ بِرَجُلٍ ضَارِبٍ أَبُوهُ بَكْرًا،
text.en: Fourth, the active participle in the sense of the present or the future does the work of the active verb, on condition that it leans on a word that is before it. That word is either a mubtadaʾ, as Zaydun qāʾimun abūhu “Zayd, his father is standing”, and with a transitive, as Zaydun ḍāribun abūhu ʿAmran “Zayd, his father is hitting ʿAmr”; or a described noun, as marartu bi-rajulin ḍāribin abūhu Bakran “I passed by a man whose father is hitting Bakr”;

text.original: یا موصول، چون جَاءَنِي الْقَائِمُ أَبُوهُ، وَجَاءَنِي الضَّارِبُ أَبُوهُ عَمْرًا، یا ذو الحال، چون جَاءَنِي زَيْدٌ رَاكِبًا غُلَامُهُ فَرَسًا، یا همزه استفهام، چون أَضَارِبٌ زَيْدٌ عَمْرًا، یا حرف نفی، چون مَا قَائِمٌ زَيْدٌ، و همان عمل که قَامَ و ضَرَبَ میکرد قَائِمٌ و ضَارِبٌ میکند.
text.en: or a relative, as jāʾanī al-qāʾimu abūhu “the one whose father is standing came to me” and wa-jāʾanī al-ḍāribu abūhu ʿAmran “and the one whose father is hitting ʿAmr came to me”; or the owner of a ḥāl, as jāʾanī Zaydun rākiban ghulāmuhu farasan “Zayd came to me, his servant riding a horse”; or the hamza of question, as a-ḍāribun Zaydun ʿAmran “is Zayd hitting ʿAmr?”; or a particle of negation, as mā qāʾimun Zaydun “Zayd is not standing”. The same work that qāma and ḍaraba did, qāʾimun and ḍāribun do.

text.original: پنجم اسم مفعول بمعنی حال و استقبال عمل فعل مجهول کند بشرط اعتماد مذکور، چون زَيْدٌ مَضْرُوبٌ أَبُوهُ، وَعَمْرٌو مُعْطًى غُلَامُهُ دِرْهَمًا، وَبَكْرٌ مَعْلُومٌ ابْنُهُ فَاضِلًا، وَخَالِدٌ مُخْبَرٌ ابْنُهُ عَمْرًا فَاضِلًا، همان عمل که ضُرِبَ و أُعْطِيَ و عُلِمَ و أُخْبِرَ میکرد مَضْرُوبٌ و مُعْطًى و مَعْلُومٌ و مُخْبَرٌ میکند.
text.en: Fifth, the passive participle in the sense of the present or the future does the work of the passive verb, on the condition of leaning mentioned, as Zaydun maḍrūbun abūhu “Zayd, his father is beaten”, wa-ʿAmrun muʿṭan ghulāmuhu dirhaman “and ʿAmr, his servant is given a dirham”, wa-Bakrun maʿlūmun ibnuhu fāḍilan “and Bakr, his son is known to be excellent” and wa-Khālidun mukhbarun ibnuhu ʿAmran fāḍilan “and Khālid, his son is told that ʿAmr is excellent”. The same work that ḍuriba, uʿṭiya, ʿulima and ukhbira did, maḍrūbun, muʿṭan, maʿlūmun and mukhbarun do.

text.original: ششم صفت مشبهه عمل فعل خود کند بشرط اعتماد مذکور، چون زَيْدٌ حَسَنٌ غُلَامُهُ، همان عمل که حَسُنَ میکرد حَسَنٌ میکند.
text.en: Sixth, the adjective like the participle (ṣifa mushabbaha) does the work of its verb, on the condition of leaning mentioned, as Zaydun ḥasanun ghulāmuhu “Zayd, his servant is handsome”. The same work that ḥasuna did, ḥasanun does.

lessons.title: The elative, the maṣdar, the muḍāf, the complete noun, kam and kadhā
lessons.arabic: اسْمُ التَّفْضِيلِ وَالْمَصْدَرُ وَالْمُضَافُ وَالِاسْمُ التَّامُّ وَالْكِنَايَاتُ
lessons.transliteration: ism al-tafḍīl wa-l-maṣdar wa-l-muḍāf wa-l-ism al-tāmm wa-l-kināyāt
body: The seventh is the elative, used in three ways: with min, Zaydun afḍalu min ʿAmrin; with al-, jāʾanī Zaydun al-afḍalu; in iḍāfa, Zaydun afḍalu al-qawmi. “Its governing is in the fāʿil, which is huwa, hidden in it”: it governs no visible noun here. The eighth is the maṣdar, which does the work of its verb, “on condition that it is not a mafʿūl muṭlaq”: aʿjabanī ḍarbu Zaydin ʿAmran, “Zayd's hitting ʿAmr pleased me”.

The ninth is the muḍāf, which puts the muḍāf ilayhi in jarr: jāʾanī ghulāmu Zaydin. “Here a lām is in truth implied”: ghulāmun li-Zaydin, “a servant belonging to Zayd”. The tenth is the complete noun (ism tāmm), which puts its tamyīz in naṣb. It is complete by tanwīn, mā fī al-samāʾi qadru rāḥatin saḥāban; by an implied tanwīn, ʿindī aḥada ʿashara rajulan, Zaydun aktharu minka mālan; by the nūn of the dual, ʿindī qafīzāni burran; by the nūn of the plural, hal unabbiʾukum bi-l-akhsarīna aʿmālan (Q 18:103); by what is like it, ʿindī ʿishrūna dirhaman, up to tisʿūna; or by iḍāfa, ʿindī milʾuhu ʿasalan, “I have its fill of honey”.

The eleventh is the allusive nouns of number, kam and kadhā. Kam is of two kinds: the asking kam puts its tamyīz in naṣb, and so does kadhā: kam rajulan ʿindaka?, ʿindī kadhā dirhaman. The telling kam (khabariyya) puts it in jarr: kam mālin anfaqtu, “how much wealth I have spent!”, kam dārin banaytu, “how many houses I have built!”; and sometimes min comes before it: wa-kam min malakin fī al-samāwāti (Q 53:26).

With these eleven, chapter three is done, and with it the verbal governors. The commentators explain the name of the tenth: the noun is “complete” because its tanwīn, its nūn or its iḍāfa leaves no room to make it muḍāf to the next word, so that word takes naṣb as a tamyīz.

the asking kam (naṣb) and the telling kam (jarr)
the implied lām of the iḍāfa: ghulāmun li-Zaydin

tasks.prompt: What does the elative govern in Zaydun afḍalu min ʿAmrin?
tasks.answer: Only its fāʿil, huwa, hidden in it. It does not govern a visible noun here.

tasks.prompt: Why can ḍarban in ḍarabtu ḍarban not govern like its verb, while ḍarbu in aʿjabanī ḍarbu Zaydin ʿAmran does?
tasks.answer: The maṣdar governs only if it is not a mafʿūl muṭlaq. Ḍarban in ḍarabtu ḍarban is a mafʿūl muṭlaq; ḍarbu is the doer of aʿjabanī, so it may govern: Zayd its doer, ʿAmr its object.

tasks.prompt: How does the tamyīz after the asking kam differ from that after the telling kam?
tasks.answer: After the asking kam it is in naṣb: kam rajulan ʿindaka? After the telling kam it is in jarr: kam mālin anfaqtu, sometimes with min.

text.original: هفتم اسم تفضیل، و استعمال او بر سه وجه است: یا بِمِنْ، چون زَيْدٌ أَفْضَلُ مِنْ عَمْرٍو، یا با الف و لام، چون جَاءَنِي زَيْدٌ الْأَفْضَلُ، یا باضافت، چون زَيْدٌ أَفْضَلُ الْقَوْمِ، و عمل او در فاعل باشد، و آن هُوَ است، فاعل أَفْضَلُ که درو مستتر است.
text.en: Seventh, the elative (ism al-tafḍīl). It is used in three ways: either with min, as Zaydun afḍalu min ʿAmrin “Zayd is better than ʿAmr”; or with the alif and lām, as jāʾanī Zaydun al-afḍalu “Zayd, the better one, came to me”; or in iḍāfa, as Zaydun afḍalu al-qawmi “Zayd is the best of the people”. Its governing is in the fāʿil, which is huwa, the fāʿil of afḍalu, hidden in it.

text.original: هشتم مصدر، بشرط آنکه مفعول مطلق نباشد، عمل فعلش کند، چون أَعْجَبَنِي ضَرْبُ زَيْدٍ عَمْرًا.
text.en: Eighth, the maṣdar, on condition that it is not a mafʿūl muṭlaq, does the work of its verb, as aʿjabanī ḍarbu Zaydin ʿAmran “Zayd's hitting ʿAmr pleased me”.

text.original: نهم اسم مضاف، مضاف الیه را جر کند، چون جَاءَنِي غُلَامُ زَيْدٍ. بدانکه اینجا لام بحقیقت مقدر است، زیرا که تقدیرش آنست که غُلَامٌ لِزَيْدٍ.
text.en: Ninth, the muḍāf noun puts the muḍāf ilayhi in jarr, as jāʾanī ghulāmu Zaydin “Zayd's servant came to me”. Know that here a lām is in truth implied, for its implied [wording] is ghulāmun li-Zaydin “a servant belonging to Zayd”.

text.original: دهم اسم تام، تمییز را نصب کند، و تمامی اسم یا بتنوین باشد، چون مَا فِي السَّمَاءِ قَدْرُ رَاحَةٍ سَحَابًا، یا بتقدیر تنوین، چون عِنْدِي أَحَدَ عَشَرَ رَجُلًا، وَزَيْدٌ أَكْثَرُ مِنْكَ مَالًا، یا بنون تثنیه، چون عِنْدِي قَفِيزَانِ بُرًّا، یا بنون جمع، چون هَلْ أُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِالْأَخْسَرِينَ أَعْمَالًا، یا بشبه نون جمع، چون عِنْدِي عِشْرُونَ دِرْهَمًا تا تِسْعُونَ، یا باضافت، چون عِنْدِي مِلْؤُهُ عَسَلًا.
text.en: Tenth, the complete noun (ism tāmm) puts the tamyīz in naṣb. The noun is complete either by tanwīn, as mā fī al-samāʾi qadru rāḥatin saḥāban “there is not in the sky [so much as] the size of a palm in clouds”; or by an implied tanwīn, as ʿindī aḥada ʿashara rajulan “I have eleven men” and wa-Zaydun aktharu minka mālan “and Zayd has more wealth than you”; or by the nūn of the dual, as ʿindī qafīzāni burran “I have two qafīzs of wheat”; or by the nūn of the plural, as hal unabbiʾukum bi-al-akhsarīna aʿmālan “shall We tell you who are the greatest losers in their deeds?” [18:103]; or by what is like the nūn of the plural, as ʿindī ʿishrūna dirhaman “I have twenty dirhams”, up to tisʿūna “ninety”; or by iḍāfa, as ʿindī milʾuhu ʿasalan “I have its fill of honey”.

text.original: یازدهم اسمای کنایات از عدد، و آن دو لفظ است: كَمْ وَكَذَا. كَمْ بر دو قسمت است: استفهامیه و خبریه. كَمْ استفهامیه تمییز را نصب کند، و كَذَا نیز، چون كَمْ رَجُلًا عِنْدَكَ، وَعِنْدِي كَذَا دِرْهَمًا، و كَمْ خبریه تمییز را جر کند، چون كَمْ مَالٍ أَنْفَقْتُ، وَكَمْ دَارٍ بَنَيْتُ، و گاهی مِنْ جاره بر تمییز كَمْ خبریه آید، چون قوله تعالی: وَكَمْ مِنْ مَلَكٍ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ.
text.en: Eleventh, the nouns that allude to number, which are two words: kam and kadhā. Kam is of two divisions: interrogative and declarative. The interrogative kam puts the tamyīz in naṣb, and so does kadhā, as kam rajulan ʿindaka “how many men are with you?” and wa-ʿindī kadhā dirhaman “and I have so many dirhams”; the declarative kam puts the tamyīz in jarr, as kam mālin anfaqtu “how much wealth I have spent!” and wa-kam dārin banaytu “and how many houses I have built!”. Sometimes the min of jarr comes on the tamyīz of the declarative kam, as His saying, Most High: wa-kam min malakin fī al-samāwāti “and how many an angel there is in the heavens” [53:26].

lessons.title: The two abstract governors
body: The abstract governors are two. The first is the beginning (ibtidāʾ), “the noun's being free of the verbal governors for the sake of attribution”: it puts the mubtadaʾ and the khabar in rafʿ: Zaydun qāʾimun. “Here one says that Zayd is a mubtadaʾ, marfūʿ by the ibtidāʾ, and qāʾim the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, marfūʿ by the ibtidāʾ.”

“Here there are other schools”, the book adds: that the ibtidāʾ governs the mubtadaʾ and the mubtadaʾ the khabar; and that each of the mubtadaʾ and the khabar governs the other. It names them and goes on; its own parsing follows the first view.

The second is the muḍāriʿ's being free of a governor of naṣb and of jazm, which puts it in rafʿ: yaḍribu Zaydun, “Zayd hits”: “here yaḍribu is marfūʿ because it is free of a governor of naṣb and of jazm”. The grammarians count this the view of the Kūfans; al-ʿAwāmil al-miʾa of ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī gives the Baṣran view instead, that the muḍāriʿ is raised by standing in the place of a noun.
“The governors are complete, praise be to God.” Every iʿrāb now has its cause: a particle, a verb, a noun, or one of these two.

being free of naṣb and jazm: the governor of the muḍāriʿ in rafʿ

text.original: بدانکه عوامل معنوی بر دو قسمت است: اول ابتدا، یعنی خالی بودن اسم از عوامل لفظیه بمعنی اسناد، مبتدا و خبر را رفع کند، چون زَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ، و اینجا گویند که زید مبتدا است مرفوع بابتدا، و قائم خبر مبتدا مرفوع بابتدا، و اینجا مذهب دیگرست: یکی آنکه ابتدا عامل است در مبتدا، و مبتدا در خبر، دیگر آنکه هر یکی از مبتدا و خبر عامل است در دیگری.
text.en: Know that the abstract governors are of two divisions. First, the beginning (ibtidāʾ), that is, the noun's being free of the verbal governors for the sake of attribution: it puts the mubtadaʾ and the khabar in rafʿ, as Zaydun qāʾimun “Zayd is standing”; and here one says that Zayd is a mubtadaʾ, marfūʿ by the ibtidāʾ, and qāʾim the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, marfūʿ by the ibtidāʾ. Here there are other schools: one, that the ibtidāʾ governs the mubtadaʾ, and the mubtadaʾ the khabar; another, that each of the mubtadaʾ and the khabar governs the other.

text.original: دوم خلو فعل مضارع از ناصب و جازم، فعل مضارع را رفع کند، چون يَضْرِبُ زَيْدٌ، اینجا يَضْرِبُ مرفوع است، زیرا که خالیست از ناصب و جازم. تمام شد عوامل بحمد الله تعالی وعونه.
text.en: Second, the muḍāriʿ verb's being free of a governor of naṣb and of jazm: it puts the muḍāriʿ verb in rafʿ, as yaḍribu Zaydun “Zayd hits”; here yaḍribu is marfūʿ because it is free of a governor of naṣb and of jazm. [Here] the governors are complete, praise be to God Most High and His help.

lessons.title: The followers; the adjective
body: The conclusion has three sections, and the first is the followers (tawābiʿ). A follower is “a word that comes second after a preceding word, with the iʿrāb of the preceding word, in one respect”; the preceding word is the followed (matbūʿ), and the follower “always agrees with the followed in iʿrāb”. They are of five sorts.

The first is the adjective (ṣifa), “a follower that indicates a meaning in the followed”, jāʾanī rajulun ʿālimun, “a learned man came to me”; or a meaning in something connected with it, jāʾanī rajulun ḥasanun ghulāmuhu, “a man whose servant is handsome”, or ʿālimun abūhu.

The first kind agrees with the followed “in ten things”: definiteness and indefiniteness, masculine and feminine, singular, dual and plural, rafʿ, naṣb and jarr. In any one phrase it agrees in four of them, one from each group: ʿindī rajulun ʿālimun, wa-rajulāni ʿālimāni, wa-rijālun ʿālimūna, wa-mraʾatun ʿālimatun, wa-mraʾatāni ʿālimatāni, wa-niswatun ʿālimātun.

The second kind, describing something connected, agrees only in definiteness and in iʿrāb: jāʾanī rajulun ʿālimun abūhu, where ʿālim is masculine singular for abūhu, though it describes rajulun. And an indefinite may be described by a declarative sentence: jāʾanī rajulun abūhu ʿālimun; the sentence must hold a pronoun back to the indefinite, the -hu of abūhu.

text.original: فصل اول: در توابع. بدانکه تابع لفظیست که دوم از لفظ سابق باشد باعراب سابق از یک جهت، و لفظ سابق را متبوع گویند، و حکم تابع آنست که همیشه در اعراب موافق متبوع باشد. و توابع پنج نوع است.
text.en: Section one: on the followers (tawābiʿ). Know that the follower is a word that comes second after a preceding word, with the iʿrāb of the preceding word, in one respect. The preceding word is called the followed (matbūʿ), and the rule of the follower is that it always agrees with the followed in iʿrāb. The followers are of five sorts.

text.original: اول صفت، و او تابعی است که دلالت کند بر معنی که در متبوع باشد، چون جَاءَنِي رَجُلٌ عَالِمٌ، یا بر معنی که در متعلق متبوع باشد، چون جَاءَنِي رَجُلٌ حَسَنٌ غُلَامُهُ، یا عَالِمٌ أَبُوهُ، مثلا.
text.en: First, the adjective (ṣifa), which is a follower that indicates a meaning that is in the followed, as jāʾanī rajulun ʿālimun “a learned man came to me”; or a meaning that is in something connected with the followed, as jāʾanī rajulun ḥasanun ghulāmuhu “a man whose servant is handsome came to me”, or ʿālimun abūhu “whose father is learned”, for example.

text.original: قسم اول در ده چیز موافق متبوع باشد: در تعریف و تنکیر و تذکیر و تأنیث و افراد و تثنیه و جمع و رفع و نصب و جر، چون عِنْدِي رَجُلٌ عَالِمٌ، وَرَجُلَانِ عَالِمَانِ، وَرِجَالٌ عَالِمُونَ، وَامْرَأَةٌ عَالِمَةٌ، وَامْرَأَتَانِ عَالِمَتَانِ، وَنِسْوَةٌ عَالِمَاتٌ.
text.en: The first division agrees with the followed in ten things: in definiteness and indefiniteness, masculine and feminine, singular, dual and plural, rafʿ, naṣb and jarr, as ʿindī rajulun ʿālimun “I have a learned man”, wa-rajulāni ʿālimāni “and two learned men”, wa-rijālun ʿālimūna “and learned men”, wa-imraʾatun ʿālimatun “and a learned woman”, wa-imraʾatāni ʿālimatāni “and two learned women” and wa-niswatun ʿālimātun “and learned women”.

text.original: قسم دوم موافق متبوع باشد در تعریف و تنکیر و رفع و نصب و جر، چون جَاءَنِي رَجُلٌ عَالِمٌ أَبُوهُ. بدانکه نکره را بجمله خبریه صفت توان کرد، چون جَاءَنِي رَجُلٌ أَبُوهُ عَالِمٌ، و در جمله ضمیری عائد بنکره لازم باشد.
text.en: The second division agrees with the followed in definiteness and indefiniteness, rafʿ, naṣb and jarr, as jāʾanī rajulun ʿālimun abūhu “a man whose father is learned came to me”. Know that an indefinite can be described by a declarative sentence, as jāʾanī rajulun abūhu ʿālimun “a man came to me whose father is learned”, and in the sentence a pronoun referring to the indefinite is necessary.

lessons.title: Emphasis (taʾkīd)
body: The second follower is emphasis (taʾkīd), “a follower that confirms the state of the followed in the attribution or in the inclusion, so that no doubt remains for the hearer”. In the attribution: was it really Zayd who came? In the inclusion: did all of them come?
Verbal emphasis repeats the word, a noun, a verb or a particle: Zaydun Zaydun qāʾimun, “Zayd, Zayd is standing”; ḍaraba ḍaraba Zaydun; inna inna Zaydan qāʾimun.

Emphasis of meaning uses eight words: nafs and ʿayn, “self”; kilā and kiltā, “both”; kull, “all”; ajmaʿ, “all”; and aktaʿ, abtaʿ and abṣaʿ, which strengthen ajmaʿ. Jāʾanī Zaydun nafsuhu; jāʾanī al-Zaydāni anfusuhumā; jāʾanī al-Zaydūna anfusuhum, and ʿayn likewise; jāʾanī al-Zaydāni kilāhumā, wa-l-Hindāni kiltāhumā, kilā and kiltā being “reserved for the dual”.

And jāʾanī al-qawmu kulluhum ajmaʿūna aktaʿūna abtaʿūna abṣaʿūna, “the people came to me, all of them, every one, the whole of them”. “Aktaʿ, abtaʿ and abṣaʿ follow ajmaʿ”: they never come without it, nor before it. The book's bracket says what they do: they strengthen ajmaʿ.

terms.en: verbal emphasis: repeating the word
emphasis of meaning: nafs, ʿayn, kilā, kiltā, kull, ajmaʿ…
the words that follow ajmaʿ and strengthen it

tasks.prompt: What doubt does each remove: jāʾanī Zaydun nafsuhu; jāʾanī al-qawmu kulluhum?
tasks.arabic: جَاءَنِي زَيْدٌ نَفْسُهُ — جَاءَنِي الْقَوْمُ كُلُّهُمْ
tasks.answer: Nafsuhu removes doubt in the attribution: it was Zayd himself who came, not his messenger. Kulluhum removes doubt in the inclusion: all of them came, not some.

tasks.answer: Jāʾanī al-Zaydāni anfusuhumā; jāʾanī al-Zaydūna anfusuhum: the plural anfus with a pronoun that agrees.

tasks.answer: No: aktaʿ, abtaʿ and abṣaʿ follow ajmaʿ; they do not come without it, nor before it.

text.original: دوم تأکید، و او تابعیست که حال متبوع را مقرر گرداند در نسبت یا در شمول، تا سامع را شک نماند. و تأکید بر دو قسمت است: لفظی و معنوی. تأکید لفظی بتکرار لفظ است، چون زَيْدٌ زَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ، وَضَرَبَ ضَرَبَ زَيْدٌ، وَإِنَّ إِنَّ زَيْدًا قَائِمٌ.
text.en: Second, the emphasis (taʾkīd), which is a follower that confirms the state of the followed in the attribution or in the inclusion, so that no doubt remains for the hearer. The taʾkīd is of two divisions: verbal (lafẓī) and of meaning (maʿnawī). The verbal taʾkīd is by repeating the word, as Zaydun Zaydun qāʾimun “Zayd, Zayd is standing”, wa-ḍaraba ḍaraba Zaydun “and Zayd hit, hit” and wa-inna inna Zaydan qāʾimun “and indeed, indeed Zayd is standing”.

text.original: و تأکید معنوی بهشت لفظ است: نَفْسٌ، وَعَيْنٌ، وَكِلَا، وَكِلْتَا، وَكُلٌّ، وَأَجْمَعُ، وَأَكْتَعُ، وَأَبْتَعُ، وَأَبْصَعُ، چون جَاءَنِي زَيْدٌ نَفْسُهُ، وَجَاءَنِي الزَّيْدَانِ أَنْفُسُهُمَا، وَجَاءَنِي الزَّيْدُونَ أَنْفُسُهُمْ، و عین را برین قیاس کن، وَجَاءَنِي الزَّيْدَانِ كِلَاهُمَا، وَالْهِنْدَانِ كِلْتَاهُمَا، و كِلَا و كِلْتَا خاص بمثنی است،
text.en: The taʾkīd of meaning is with eight words: nafsun “self”, ʿaynun “self”, kilā and kiltā “both”, kullun “all”, ajmaʿu “all”, and aktaʿu, abtaʿu and abṣaʿu [which strengthen ajmaʿ], as jāʾanī Zaydun nafsuhu “Zayd himself came to me”, wa-jāʾanī al-Zaydāni anfusuhumā “and the two Zayds themselves came to me” and wa-jāʾanī al-Zaydūna anfusuhum “and the Zayds themselves came to me” — judge ʿayn by this —; wa-jāʾanī al-Zaydāni kilāhumā “and the two Zayds came to me, both of them” and wa-al-Hindāni kiltāhumā “and the two Hinds, both of them”; kilā and kiltā are reserved for the dual;

text.original: وَجَاءَنِي الْقَوْمُ كُلُّهُمْ أَجْمَعُونَ أَكْتَعُونَ أَبْتَعُونَ أَبْصَعُونَ. بدانکه أَكْتَعُ و أَبْتَعُ و أَبْصَعُ اتباع أَجْمَعُ اند، پس بدون أَجْمَعُ و مقدم بر أَجْمَعُ نباشند.
text.en: and wa-jāʾanī al-qawmu kulluhum ajmaʿūna aktaʿūna abtaʿūna abṣaʿūna “and the people came to me, all of them, every one, the whole of them”. Know that aktaʿu, abtaʿu and abṣaʿu follow ajmaʿu; so they do not come without ajmaʿu, nor before ajmaʿu.

lessons.title: The substitute, the joining by a particle, the explicative apposition
body: The third follower is the substitute (badal), “a follower that is what is intended by the attribution”. It has four kinds in this book. The badal of the whole, whose meaning is the meaning of what it replaces: jāʾanī Zaydun akhūka, “Zayd, your brother, came to me”. The badal of the part: ḍuriba Zaydun raʾsuhu, “Zayd was struck, his head”.

The badal of inclusion, whose meaning is connected with what it replaces: suliba Zaydun thawbuhu, “Zayd was robbed, his garment”. And the badal of mistake, “mentioned with another word after a mistake”: marartu bi-rajulin ḥimārin, “I passed by a man — a donkey”, where the speaker meant the donkey and the man was a slip.

The fourth follower is the joining by a particle (ʿaṭf bi-ḥarf, also ʿaṭf al-nasaq), “a follower that is intended by the attribution together with what it follows, after a particle of ʿaṭf”: jāʾanī Zaydun wa-ʿAmrun. Both came. Its ten particles come in the third section of the conclusion.

The fifth is the explicative apposition (ʿaṭf al-bayān), “a follower, not an adjective, that makes the followed clear”: aqsama bi-llāhi Abū Ḥafṣin ʿUmaru, when the name is better known than the kunya; and jāʾanī Zaydun Abū ʿAmrin, when the kunya is better known. Whichever is better known comes second to make the first clear.

text.original: سوم بدل، و او تابعیست که مقصود بنسبت او باشد، و بدل بر چهار قسم است: بدل الکل، و بدل البعض، و بدل الاشتمال، و بدل الغلط.
text.en: Third, the substitute (badal), which is a follower that is what is intended by the attribution. The badal is of four divisions: the badal of the whole (badal al-kull), the badal of the part (badal al-baʿḍ), the badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl) and the badal of mistake (badal al-ghalaṭ).

text.original: بدل الکل آنست که مدلولش مدلول مبدل منه باشد، چون جَاءَنِي زَيْدٌ أَخُوكَ، و بدل البعض آنست که مدلولش جزو مبدل منه باشد، چون ضُرِبَ زَيْدٌ رَأْسُهُ، و بدل الاشتمال آنست که مدلولش متعلق بمبدل منه باشد، چون سُلِبَ زَيْدٌ ثَوْبُهُ، و بدل الغلط آنست که بعد از غلط بلفظ دیگر یاد کنند، چون مَرَرْتُ بِرَجُلٍ حِمَارٍ.
text.en: The badal of the whole is that whose meaning is the meaning of what it replaces (mubdal minhu), as jāʾanī Zaydun akhūka “Zayd, your brother, came to me”. The badal of the part is that whose meaning is a part of the mubdal minhu, as ḍuriba Zaydun raʾsuhu “Zayd was struck, his head”. The badal of inclusion is that whose meaning is connected with the mubdal minhu, as suliba Zaydun thawbuhu “Zayd was robbed, his garment”. The badal of mistake is that which is mentioned with another word after a mistake, as marartu bi-rajulin ḥimārin “I passed by a man — a donkey”.

text.original: چهارم عطف بحرف، و او تابعیست که مقصود باشد بنسبت با متبوعش بعد از حرف عطف، چون جَاءَنِي زَيْدٌ وَعَمْرٌو، و حروف عطف ده است، در فصل سوم یاد کنیم ان شاء الله تعالی، و او را عطف نسق نیز گویند.
text.en: Fourth, the joining by a particle (ʿaṭf bi-ḥarf), which is a follower that is intended by the attribution together with what it follows, after a particle of ʿaṭf, as jāʾanī Zaydun wa-ʿAmrun “Zayd and ʿAmr came to me”. The particles of ʿaṭf are ten; we shall mention them in the third section, God Most High willing. It is also called ʿaṭf al-nasaq.

text.original: پنجم عطف بیان، و او تابعیست غیر صفت که متبوع را روشن گرداند، چون أَقْسَمَ بِاللَّهِ أَبُو حَفْصٍ عُمَرُ، وقتیکه علم مشهورتر باشد، وَجَاءَنِي زَيْدٌ أَبُو عَمْرٍو، وقتیکه کنیت مشهورتر باشد.
text.en: Fifth, the explicative apposition (ʿaṭf al-bayān), which is a follower, not an adjective, that makes the followed clear, as aqsama bi-Allāhi Abū Ḥafṣin ʿUmaru “Abū Ḥafṣ ʿUmar swore by God”, when the name is better known, and wa-jāʾanī Zaydun Abū ʿAmrin “and Zayd Abū ʿAmr came to me”, when the kunya is better known.

lessons.title: Conclusion, section two: the munṣarif and the ghayr munṣarif
body: The munṣarif is a noun with none of the causes that keep it from tanwīn; the ghayr munṣarif has two of them. The causes are nine: deflection (ʿadl), the adjective, femininity, definiteness (being a proper name), foreignness, the plural, the compound, the pattern of the verb, and the added alif and nūn. Lesson 15 showed its iʿrāb: rafʿ with the ḍamma, naṣb and jarr with the fatḥa.

The book gives a word for each pair. ʿUmaru: deflection and being a proper name. Thulāthu and mathlathu, “three by three”: the adjective and deflection. Ṭalḥatu: femininity and being a proper name. Zaynabu: femininity of meaning and being a proper name. Ḥublā and ḥamrāʾu: femininity by the short and the long alif, “and this femininity stands in the place of two causes”.

Ibrāhīmu: foreignness and being a proper name. Masājidu and maṣābīḥu: “the furthest plural” (muntahā al-jumūʿ), which also stands in the place of two causes. Baʿlabakku: the compound and being a proper name. Aḥmadu: the pattern of the verb and being a proper name. Sakrānu: the added alif and nūn and the adjective. ʿUthmānu: the added alif and nūn and being a proper name.

“The full study of the ghayr munṣarif is to be learnt from other books.” The beginner should take two things from here: the list of nine, and that two causes are needed, except where one, the alif of the feminine or the furthest plural, counts as two.

text.original: فصل دوم: در بیان منصرف و غیر منصرف. منصرف آنست که هیچ سبب از اسباب منع صرف در وی نباشد، و غیر منصرف آنست که دو سبب از اسباب منع صرف در وی باشد. و اسباب منع صرف نه است: عدل و وصف و تأنیث و معرفه و عجمه و جمع و ترکیب و وزن فعل و الف و نون مزیدتان،
text.en: Section two: on the munṣarif and the ghayr munṣarif. The munṣarif is that in which there is none of the causes that keep a noun from tanwīn, and the ghayr munṣarif is that in which there are two of the causes that keep it from tanwīn. The causes are nine: deflection (ʿadl), the adjective (waṣf), femininity (taʾnīth), definiteness (maʿrifa), foreignness (ʿujma), the plural (jamʿ), the compound (tarkīb), the pattern of the verb (wazn al-fiʿl), and the added alif and nūn;

text.original: چنانچه در عُمَرُ عدل است و علم، و در ثُلَاثُ و مَثْلَثُ صفت است و عدل، و در طَلْحَةُ تأنیث است و علم، و در زَيْنَبُ تأنیث معنوی و علم، و در حُبْلَى تأنیث است بالف مقصوره، و در حَمْرَاءُ تأنیث است بالف ممدوده، و این تأنیث بجای دو سبب است،
text.en: as in ʿUmaru ʿUmar there are deflection and being a proper name; in thulāthu and mathlathu “three by three” the adjective and deflection; in Ṭalḥatu Ṭalḥa femininity and being a proper name; in Zaynabu Zaynab femininity of meaning and being a proper name; in ḥublā “pregnant” femininity by the short alif; and in ḥamrāʾu “red (f.)” femininity by the long alif; and this femininity stands in the place of two causes;

text.original: و در إِبْرَاهِيمُ عجمه است و علم، و در مَسَاجِدُ وَمَصَابِيحُ جمع منتهی الجموع بجای دو سبب است، و در بَعْلَبَكُّ ترکیب است و علم، و در أَحْمَدُ وزن فعل است و علم، و در سَكْرَانُ الف و نون زائدتان است و وصف، و در عُثْمَانُ الف و نون زائدتان است و علم. و تحقیق غیر منصرف از کتب دیگر معلوم شود.
text.en: in Ibrāhīmu Ibrāhīm there are foreignness and being a proper name; in masājidu “mosques” and maṣābīḥu “lamps” the furthest plural (muntahā al-jumūʿ), standing in the place of two causes; in Baʿlabakku Baalbek the compound and being a proper name; in Aḥmadu Aḥmad the pattern of the verb and being a proper name; in sakrānu “drunk” the added alif and nūn and the adjective; and in ʿUthmānu ʿUthmān the added alif and nūn and being a proper name. The full study of the ghayr munṣarif is to be learnt from other books.

parts.title: Conclusion: the particles that do not govern

lessons.title: Conclusion, section three: the particles that do not govern (1)
body: The last section is the particles that do not govern, in sixteen kinds. First, the particles of alerting (tanbīh): alā, amā, hā. Second, of affirming (ījāb), “yes”: naʿam, balā, ajal, ī, jayri, inna. Third, of explaining (tafsīr), “that is”: ay and an, as wa-nādaynāhu an yā Ibrāhīmu, “and We called to him: O Abraham!” (Q 37:104), where an explains what the call was.

Fourth, the maṣdar-making particles, mā, an and anna; mā and an go on the verb so that it has the sense of a maṣdar. Fifth, the particles of urging (taḥḍīḍ), allā, hallā, lawlā, lawmā, “why not?”. Sixth, the particle of expectation (tawaqquʿ), qad: in the past for confirming, or for bringing the past near to the present; in the muḍāriʿ for lessening, “sometimes”. Seventh, the particles of question: mā, the hamza and hal. Eighth, the particle of rebuke (radʿ), kallā, “no!”, turning the hearer back, and sometimes “truly”: kallā sawfa taʿlamūna, “nay, you will come to know” (Q 102:3).

Ninth, tanwīn, of five kinds. Of firm placing (tamakkun), Zaydun; the commentators explain it as the mark of a fully inflected noun, and they explain the next three likewise. Of indefiniteness (tankīr), ṣahin, “be silent some silence at some time”, against ṣah without tanwīn, “be silent now”: the tanwīn makes the noun of a verb indefinite. Of compensation (ʿiwaḍ), yawmaʾidhin, “on that day”, the tanwīn standing, they say, for a dropped sentence. Of correspondence (muqābala), muslimātin, answering the nūn of muslimūna.

And of singing (tarannum), at the end of verses: aqillī al-lawma ʿādhila wa-l-ʿitāban / wa-qūlī in aṣabtu la-qad aṣāban, “lessen the blame, O blamer, and the reproach, and say, if I am right: he has been right”. “The tanwīn of singing goes on the noun, the verb and the particle” (aṣāban is a verb); the first four are reserved for the noun.

tasks.prompt: What does an do in wa-nādaynāhu an yā Ibrāhīmu?
tasks.answer: It is the particle of explaining (tafsīr), “that is”: it explains what the call was, “O Abraham!”. It governs nothing.

tasks.prompt: What is the difference between ṣahin and ṣah?
tasks.answer: Ṣah without tanwīn means “be silent the silence now”, a particular silence. Ṣahin with the tanwīn of indefiniteness means “be silent some silence at some time”.

tasks.prompt: What does qad do in the past and in the muḍāriʿ?
tasks.answer: In the past it confirms, or brings the past near to the present (qad ḍaraba, “he has hit”). In the muḍāriʿ it lessens: “sometimes”.

text.original: فصل سوم: در حروف غیر عامله، و آن شانزده قسمت است. اول حروف تنبیه، و آن سه است: أَلَا، وَأَمَا، وَهَا. دوم حروف ایجاب، و آن شش است: نَعَمْ، وَبَلَى، وَأَجَلْ، وَإِي، وَجَيْرِ، وَإِنَّ. سوم حروف تفسیر، و آن دو است: أَيْ وَأَنْ، کقوله تعالی: وَنَادَيْنَاهُ أَنْ يَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ.
text.en: Section three: on the particles that do not govern; they are of sixteen divisions. First, the particles of alerting (tanbīh), which are three: alā, amā and hā. Second, the particles of affirming (ījāb), which are six: naʿam, balā, ajal, ī, jayri and inna “yes”. Third, the particles of explaining (tafsīr), which are two: ay and an “that is”, as His saying, Most High: wa-nādaynāhu an yā Ibrāhīmu “and We called to him: O Abraham!” [37:104].

text.original: چهارم حروف مصدریه، و آن سه است: مَا، وَأَنْ، وَأَنَّ؛ مَا و أَنْ در فعل روند تا فعل بمعنی مصدر باشد. پنجم حروف تحضیض، و آن چهار است: أَلَّا، وَهَلَّا، وَلَوْلَا، وَلَوْمَا. ششم حرف توقع، و آن قَدْ است، برای تحقیق در ماضی، و برای تقریب ماضی بحال، و در مضارع برای تقلیل.
text.en: Fourth, the maṣdar-making particles, which are three: mā, an and anna; mā and an go on the verb, so that the verb has the sense of a maṣdar. Fifth, the particles of urging (taḥḍīḍ), which are four: allā, hallā, lawlā and lawmā “why not?”. Sixth, the particle of expectation (tawaqquʿ), which is qad: for confirming in the past, for bringing the past near to the present, and in the muḍāriʿ for lessening.

text.original: هفتم حروف استفهام، و آن سه است: مَا، و همزه، و هَلْ. هشتم حرف ردع، و آن كَلَّا است، بمعنی باز گردانیدن، و بمعنی حَقًّا نیز آمده است، چون كَلَّا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ.
text.en: Seventh, the particles of question, which are three: mā, the hamza and hal. Eighth, the particle of rebuke (radʿ), which is kallā, in the sense of turning [someone] back; it has also come in the sense of ḥaqqan “truly”, as kallā sawfa taʿlamūna “nay, you will come to know” [102:3].

text.original: نهم تنوین، و آن پنج است: تمکن، چون زَيْدٌ، و تنکیر، چون صَهٍ، أَيِ اسْكُتْ سُكُوتًا مَا فِي وَقْتٍ مَا، و صَهْ بغیر تنوین مَعْنَاهُ اُسْكُتِ السُّكُوتَ الْآنَ، و عوض، چون يَوْمَئِذٍ، و مقابله، چون مُسْلِمَاتٍ، و ترنم، که در آخر ابیات باشد، شعر: أَقِلِّي اللَّوْمَ عَاذِلَ وَالْعِتَابَنْ * وَقُولِي إِنْ أَصَبْتُ لَقَدْ أَصَابَنْ. و تنوین ترنم در اسم و فعل و حرف رود، اما چهار اولین خاص است باسم.
text.en: Ninth, tanwīn, which is five [kinds]: of firm placing (tamakkun), as Zaydun; of indefiniteness (tankīr), as ṣahin, ayi uskut sukūtan mā fī waqtin mā “that is, be silent some silence at some time”, while ṣah without tanwīn maʿnāhu uskuti al-sukūta al-āna “means: be silent the silence now”; of compensation (ʿiwaḍ), as yawmaʾidhin “on that day”; of correspondence (muqābala), as muslimātin “Muslim women”; and of singing (tarannum), which is at the end of verses, [as in the] verse: aqillī al-lawma ʿādhila wa-al-ʿitāban / wa-qūlī in aṣabtu la-qad aṣāban “lessen the blame, O blamer, and the reproach, and say, if I am right: he has been right”. The tanwīn of singing goes on the noun, the verb and the particle, but the first four are reserved for the noun.

lessons.title: Conclusion, section three: the particles that do not govern (2)
body: Tenth, the nūn of emphasis at the end of the muḍāriʿ verb, heavy and light: iḍribanna and iḍriban, “do hit!”. Eleventh, the particles of addition (ziyāda), eight: in, an, mā, lā, min, the kāf, the bāʾ and the lām. “The rest of the account was given under the particles of jarr”: the book does not repeat it here.

Twelfth, the particles of condition that do not govern, ammā and law. Ammā is “for setting out in detail”, and its answer must take the fāʾ: fa-minhum shaqiyyun wa-saʿīdun. fa-ammā alladhīna shaqū fa-fī al-nāri … wa-ammā alladhīna suʿidū fa-fī al-jannati (Q 11:105–108). Law is “for the second's not being because the first is not”: law kāna fīhimā ālihatun illā Allāhu la-fasadatā, “had there been gods in them other than God, they would both have been ruined” (Q 21:22): they are not ruined, because there are no such gods.

Thirteenth, lawlā, the reverse of law: “for the second's not being because the first is”: lawlā ʿAliyyun la-halaka ʿUmaru, “were it not for ʿAlī, ʿUmar would have perished”: ʿUmar did not perish, because ʿAlī was there. Fourteenth, the lām with fatḥa for emphasis: la-Zaydun afḍalu min ʿAmrin. Fifteenth, mā in the sense of mā dāma: aqūmu mā jalasa al-amīru, “I will stand as long as the emir sits”.

Sixteenth, the particles of ʿaṭf, ten: wa-, fa-, thumma, ḥattā, immā, aw, am, lā, bal and lākin, which the chapter of the followers promised. With them the book ends, “tammat”: from the word to the sentence, from the sentence to its governors, and back to the particles that govern nothing but still give the sentence its sense.

text.original: دهم نون تأکید در آخر فعل مضارع، ثقیله و خفیفه، چون اِضْرِبَنَّ اِضْرِبَنْ. یازدهم حروف زیادت، و آن هشت حرف است: إِنْ، وَأَنْ، وَمَا، وَلَا، وَمِنْ، و کاف، و با، و لام، و بیان آخر در حرف جر یاد کرده شد.
text.en: Tenth, the nūn of emphasis at the end of the muḍāriʿ verb, heavy and light, as iḍribanna and iḍriban “do hit!”. Eleventh, the particles of addition (ziyāda), which are eight letters: in, an, mā, lā, min, the kāf, the bāʾ and the lām; and the rest of the account was given under the particles of jarr.

text.original: دوازدهم حروف شرط، و آن دو است: أَمَّا وَلَوْ. أَمَّا برای تفصیل، و فا در جوابش لازم باشد، کقوله تعالی: فَمِنْهُمْ شَقِيٌّ وَسَعِيدٌ، فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ شَقُوا فَفِي النَّارِ، وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ سُعِدُوا فَفِي الْجَنَّةِ. و لَوْ برای انتفای ثانی بسبب انتفای اول، چون لَوْ كَانَ فِيهِمَا آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتَا.
text.en: Twelfth, the particles of condition, which are two: ammā and law. Ammā is for setting out in detail, and the fāʾ is necessary in its answer, as His saying, Most High: fa-minhum shaqiyyun wa-saʿīdun “and of them some will be wretched and some happy” [11:105], fa-ammā alladhīna shaqū fa-fī al-nāri “as for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire” [11:106], wa-ammā alladhīna suʿidū fa-fī al-jannati “and as for those who are made happy, they will be in the Garden” [11:108]. Law is for the second's not being because the first is not, as law kāna fīhimā ālihatun illā Allāhu la-fasadatā “had there been gods in them other than God, they would both have been ruined” [21:22].

text.original: سیزدهم لَوْلَا، و او موضوعست برای انتفای ثانی بسبب وجود اول، چون لَوْلَا عَلِيٌّ لَهَلَكَ عُمَرُ. چهاردهم لام مفتوحه برای تأکید، چون لَزَيْدٌ أَفْضَلُ مِنْ عَمْرٍو. پانزدهم مَا بمعنی مَا دَامَ، چون أَقُومُ مَا جَلَسَ الْأَمِيرُ. شانزدهم حروف عطف، و آن ده است: واو، و فا، و ثُمَّ، و حَتَّى، و إِمَّا، و أَوْ، و أَمْ، و لَا، و بَلْ، و لٰكِنْ. تمت.
text.en: Thirteenth, lawlā, which is laid down for the second's not being because the first is, as lawlā ʿAliyyun la-halaka ʿUmaru “were it not for ʿAlī, ʿUmar would have perished”. Fourteenth, the lām with fatḥa for emphasis, as la-Zaydun afḍalu min ʿAmrin “Zayd is surely better than ʿAmr”. Fifteenth, mā in the sense of mā dāma “as long as”, as aqūmu mā jalasa al-amīru “I will stand as long as the emir sits”. Sixteenth, the particles of ʿaṭf, which are ten: the wāw, the fāʾ, thumma, ḥattā, immā, aw, am, lā, bal and lākin. The end.
